papers.title: Equivariant generating hypotheses for finite groups
papers.abstract:
We prove that no nontrivial finite group $G$ satisfies the equivariant generating hypothesis of Bohmann, even when all $RO(H)$-graded homotopy groups are tested for every subgroup $H\leq G$. For each $G$, we construct ghosts on finite $G$-spectra with arbitrarily long nonzero composition powers. We also prove that the homotopy-module functors are nonfull and construct non-equivalent finite $G$-spectra with isomorphic full homotopy modules.
  A central ingredient of our proof is the natural ghost operation $\Psi=(p-[C_p/e])(1-g)$ on $C_p$-spectra. Motivated by Ma--Xu's examples in the motivic settings, we apply this operation to both a two-cell complex and products of complex projective spaces with cyclic permutation action, which produces arbitrarily long nonzero ghost powers. We also construct a ghost on an explicit four-cell complex that is detected in the derived category over the group ring.

papers.title: Straightening for lax transformations and adjunctions of $(\infty,2)$-categories
papers.abstract: We prove an unstraightening result for lax transformations between functors from an arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-category to that of $(\infty,2)$-categories. We apply this to study partially (op)lax and weighted (co)limits, giving fibrational descriptions of such (co)limits for diagrams valued in $(\infty,2)$-categories, to characterize adjoints in $(\infty,2)$-categories of functors and (op)lax transformations, and to prove a mate correspondence between lax transformations that are componentwise right adjoints and oplax transformations that are componentwise left adjoints, for such transformations among functors between arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-categories.

papers.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
papers.abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.

papers.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[
  I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$.
  We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.

papers.title: Models for dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories III: Univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and unitarily complete dagger Segal anima
papers.abstract: We identify the $(\infty,1)$-category presented by the dagger Bergner, dagger Joyal, and dagger Rezk models of Parts I and II with that of univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories. We first construct a realization--nerve adjunction between reversal simplicial anima and Hermitian flags. We prove that its nerve restricts to an equivalence between flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and dagger Segal anima, under which univalence corresponds to unitary completeness. We then construct the adjunctions for univalentization and Hermitian completion and identify univalentization with unitary completion.

papers.title: Generalized Thom Spectra, Conjugate Stacks, and truncated Brown-Peterson Spectra
papers.abstract: We propose a of definition conjugate stack for a class of suitable $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-algebras that includes the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle$ for all heights $n$. Then we calculate part of $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle^{\mathrm{conj}}$ as a quotient stack in terms of Witt vectors. To perform this computation we study generalized Thom spectra and their relative Topological Hochschild Homology. We exhibit the Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectrum $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{F}_2$ as a $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectrum, the $p$-local Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ (except for $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/4$) and $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ as $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}_{(p)}$-Thom spectra, and the connective complex K-theory spectrum $ku$ as $\mathbb{E}_1$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectra. We accompany these ``go" results with ``no-go" results that show these ``go" results do not admit $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-refinements.

papers.title: Hanslick's Musical Formalism as a Mathematical Structure - Examining meaning in Music through the Lens of Category Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate Eduard Hanslicks formalist aesthetics through the prism of Category Theory

papers.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras
papers.abstract:
We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic.
  The proof that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial uses the rational models for the Becker--Gottlieb and THH transfers obtained in previous work of the authors. In the appendix, we provide a second, more involved, proof that relies on constructing explicit $C_\infty$-algebra models for odd spherical fibrations (including circle bundles), which might be of independent interest.
  Concurrently, another counterexample (of very different flavor) was found by Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, and the first author.

papers.title: A Note on Laminar Presentations and Finite Chain Models for Ample Groupoid Homology
papers.abstract: A finite free chain model for the homology of a Hausdorff ample groupoid \(G\) is cut out of the Matui complex by a finite clopen partition of each nerve space. We ask what such a model must supply and isolate three requirements: a single model that is a quasi-isomorphism, a chain of models that is a complete system with ranks and transition maps read off the presenting data, and a bound on the number of atoms in terms of the presenting cover. An \(n\)-Helly axiom on the presenting covers supplies none of them, being satisfied by every finite atomization for every \(n\), and a \(1\)-Helly family of \(N\) compact open sets can have \(2^{N}-1\) atoms. We show that a laminar presentation, a laminar basis of compact open sets in each nerve degree, supplies the third, and the second as soon as it is countable: the atoms of a finite laminar family are exactly its nonempty nodes, so a subordinate model has rank at most the number of members presenting it, the subordinate models of finite height form a complete system containing, for a countable presentation, a chain that is itself complete, and the transition maps are the least-ancestor maps of the presenting subfamilies. Every second countable Hausdorff ample groupoid admits one, and the choice is made in each nerve degree separately, laminarity not being stable under products. The first requirement is a restriction on \(G\): the homology of a model is finitely generated over a Noetherian ring, whereas \(H_0\) over \(\mathbb Z\) is not for the unit groupoid on a Cantor set or for the CAR groupoid, and a truncated model carries free homology of arbitrary rank in arbitrarily high odd degree where the groupoid has none. The chain-level statements are accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization.

papers.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers
papers.abstract: We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$. The original proof used the amenability of the images of sufficiently small local fundamental groups. Since that work was written, Kapovitch and Wilking proved Gromov's generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Their theorem gives the stronger conclusion that these local groups are uniformly virtually nilpotent. We explain how their result supplies a direct modern input for the bounded Betti number theorem. We also discuss the topological meaning of the bounded part of ordinary cohomology and its relation to the $\ell^1$-seminorm on homology.

papers.title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
papers.abstract: Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator. This relation is precisely the condition for cyclic compatibility on the associativity morphism, giving a new proof that $\mathsf{GRT}_1$ acts by cyclic automorphisms of parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams.

papers.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
papers.abstract: Persistent homology summarizes the topological evolution of a graph as persistence diagrams (PDs). Generating graphs whose topology matches a target descriptor is increasingly important, yet existing topology-aware generative models rely on soft regularization, producing graphs whose PDs may only be approximately similar. We initiate a principled investigation of the generation problem: produce graphs that realize a target PD exactly. We propose two approaches guided by the implicit local and global constraints a target PD imposes. The local approach builds degree-based PD-equivalent graphs iteratively, and we prove that every output realizes the target PD and that every degree-based PD-equivalent graph is reachable. However, as shown thereafter, local generation necessarily trades off between sample diversity and reaching infeasible states. We therefore recast generation as a global constraint satisfaction problem with a complete encoding solvable by modern constraint programming solvers. This is applicable to any vertex-based permutation equivariant filtration scheme and is minimal under the degree filtration. Experiments on four standard graph generation benchmarks confirm that both methods realize the target PD exactly. Together, our methods provide a principled treatment of strict topology-compliant graph generation. Code is available at https://github.com/Aalto-QuML/ExactCompliance.

papers.title: Groups with the fixed-point property
papers.abstract:
We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions.
  Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.

papers.title: The Becker--Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example based on units of group rings
papers.abstract: We show by explicit counterexample that the Becker--Gottlieb transfer cannot be made functorial. A different counterexample using rational homotopy theory was discovered concurrently by the third author and Robin Stoll.

papers.title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples
papers.abstract:
The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers. For every $k\ge0$, the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers using rationals of $\Ind(\KG(3,k))$ are \[
  \beta_6=\binom{k+5}{7}+29\binom{k+6}{7}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \beta_9=\binom{k+6}{6}. \] The proof uses an inductive decomposition based on a simplicial retraction and Barmak's star clusters, Dowker duality together with Jonsson's computation of the homology of complexes of graphs with bounded covering number, and a relative Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence which reduces the problem to the six-element sets.

papers.title: $\ell$-Independence, slopes, and weights of $\ell$-adic cohomology groups of rigid spaces
papers.abstract: Let $\ell$ and $p$ be distinct prime numbers, $K$ a local field with residue characteristic $p$, $C$ a complete algebraically closed extension of $K$, and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid space over $K$. When $\mathop{\mathrm{char}} K = 0$, we prove that the alternating sum of traces of elements in the positive part of the Weil group acting on $R\Gamma(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$ is independent of $\ell$ and is an integer, extending a result of Mieda to the singular case. We also give optimal bounds for the $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius liftings acting on $H^i(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$, proving a conjecture of Lu--Zheng. In the general case, we give optimal bounds for the $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius liftings acting on $H^i_c(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$, and we show that these eigenvalues are algebraic integers and Weil numbers, thereby extending results of Lu--Zheng and Mieda to the positive characteristic case.

papers.title: $\sqrt{\Delta}$-Fine Rings
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the so-termed {\it $\sqrt{\Delta}$-fine rings}, a new class of rings that generalizes the classical {\it fine rings} introduced by C\u{a}lug\u{a}reanu-Lam in J. Algebra \& Appl. (2016) by requiring that every nonzero element $r \in R$ can be written as $r = u + a$, where $u$ is a unit and $a \in \sqrt{\Delta(R)}$. We establish that every such ring is simple, every abelian $\sqrt{\Delta}$-fine ring is indecomposable, and most notably, the matrix ring $M_n(R)$ over a $\sqrt{\Delta}$-fine ring $R$ is again $\sqrt{\Delta}$-fine for every $n \ge 1$. As a consequence, we characterize all semi-local $\sqrt{\Delta}$-fine rings as those rings which are precisely the simple Artinian rings. We also examine group rings, providing conditions under which they are either $\sqrt{\Delta}$-fine or generalized fine, where the latter class was introduced by Zhou in J. Algebra \& Appl. (2022), and conclude our work with the difficult open question asking of whether each $\sqrt{\Delta}$-fine ring is necessarily fine.

papers.title: $a$-Numbers, higher Cartier ranks and maximality of van der Geer-van der Vlugt curves
papers.abstract:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $C_R$ be the van der Geer-van der Vlugt curve $y^p-y=xR(x)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, where $R(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{h}a_ix^{p^i}$ is an additive polynomial of degree $p^h$. We determine the image and the rank of every power of the Cartier operator $\Cart$ on $H^0(C_R,\Omg)$. For $1\le r\le h-1$ the image of $\Cart^r$ is spanned by an explicit set of monomial differentials that does not depend on $R$, and $ank(\Cart^r)=p^{h-r-1} inom{p+r}{r+2}$. The last iterate detects the linear coefficient: $ank(\Cart^h)=0$ if $a_0=0$ and $ank(\Cart^h)= inom{(p-1)/2+h}{h+1}$ if $a_0
eq0$, so the nilpotency index of $\Cart$ is $h$ or $h+1$. Hence, for $h\ge2$, the loci $a_0=0$ and $a_0
e0$ have the same $a$-number, which is the largest $a$-number of a one-point Artin-Schreier curve with pole order $p^h+1$, but they share no Ekedahl-Oort type. Over finite fields we deduce that a curve over $\F_{p^{2n}}$ that is geometrically isomorphic to $C_R$ can be $\F_{p^{2n}}$-maximal or $\F_{p^{2n}}$-minimal only if $n\ge h$, and only if $n\ge h+1$ when $a_0
eq0$. Explicit examples show that the second bound is attained for $(p,h)=(3,1)$, $(3,2)$ and $(5,2)$.

papers.title: A Bogomolov property for moduli spaces of polynomials over abelian extensions
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq2$ be an integer, and let $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ be the moduli space of degree-$d$ polynomials. For every number field $K$, we prove that there exists $\epsilon_{K,d}>0$ such that \[ \left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)<\epsilon_{K,d}\right\rbrace=\left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)=0\right\rbrace \] is finite, where $h_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the critical height. In particular, only finitely many $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$-rational points of $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ are postcritically finite. The proof combines the correspondence method of Ji--Song--Xie with local ramification estimates and the uniform finiteness of intertwined classes in $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$. We also prove an analogous finiteness theorem for non-preperiodic marked points in non-isotrivial one-parameter polynomial families.

papers.title: A Category-theoretic Reconstruction of Logical Expressivism
papers.abstract: In the philosophical tradition of `analytic pragmatism', which attempts to account for linguistic meanings in terms of their practices of use, logical expressivism is a theory which offers a distinct perspective on logic. We shed light on Brandom and Hlobil's recent formalization of logical expressivism by reconstructing its formal semantics through the use of universal constructions. This reveals similarities with categorical logic: there is a focus on internalizing judgment structure, and connectives arise from adjunctions.

papers.title: A codimension formula for intrinsic perturbation of $A$-hypergeometric series
papers.abstract: We study the canonical formal solution space of a homogeneous $A$-hypergeometric system in a generic direction. We present as a finite-dimensional cokernel the quotient of that space by the span of the series obtained by intrinsic perturbation, taken over all exponents occurring in that space and all ordered negative support families, and we compute the codimension of that span. We show that the presentation and the codimension transfer to the holomorphic solutions on a common nonsingular domain. We apply these results, for every integer $q\geq 1$, to a homogeneous $A$-hypergeometric system of lattice rank 2 with $5q$ columns. We show that the canonical formal solution space of this system has dimension $12q^2$ and that the span of the series obtained by intrinsic perturbation has codimension exactly $\lceil 3q^2/4\rceil$ in that space.

papers.title: A Compositional Account of Generalized Reversible Computing
papers.abstract: We develop a compositional framework for generalized reversible computing using copy-discard categories and resource theories. We introduce partitioned matrices between partitioned sets as subdistribution matrices which preserve the equivalence relation of its domain. We model computational and physical transformations as subdistribution matrices over the category of sets and partitioned matrices on partitioned sets, respectively. We show that the interactions between the physical and computational transformations are governed by an aggregation functor whose functoriality and monoidality we deduce from general principles of the formal theory of monads. We study the associated copy-discard structures, in particular, general conditions for determinism and partial invertibility. We then define several notions of entropies that we use to state and prove the fundamental theorem of generalized reversible computing.

papers.title: A fixed point theorem for the action of linear higher rank algebraic groups over local fields on symmetric spaces of infinite dimension and finite rank
papers.abstract: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero whose residue field has at least three elements. Let G be an almost simple linear algebraic group over F, with rank_F(G) >= 2. Let X be a simply connected symmetric space of infinite dimension and finite rank, with non-positive curvature operator. We prove that every continuous action by isometries of G on X has a fixed point. If the group G contains SL_3(F), the result holds without any assumption on the non-archimedean local field F. The result extends to cocompact lattices in G if the cardinality of the residue field of F is large enough, with a bound that depends on rank_F(G).

papers.title: A Geometric Interpretation of Generalized Hurwitz--Radon Numbers Defined by Kannaka--Tojo
papers.abstract:
The Hurwitz--Radon number originates in the composition problem of quadratic forms and is related to the maximum number of pointwise linearly independent vector fields on spheres. Kannaka--Tojo [arXiv:2602.04544] reformulated the Hurwitz--Radon number in the setting of a real reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ and its faithful representation $\iota$, and introduced two natural numbers $ho^{(1)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$ and $ho^{(2)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$. For classical Lie algebras and their standard representations, these two numbers coincide except for a few cases.
  In this paper, fixing a Lie group $G$ and a subspace $\mathfrak{s} $ of $ \mathfrak g = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$ , we define natural numbers $ho_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma)$ and $ho^{\pm}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma,
abla)$ for a $G$-manifold $(M,\sigma)$ equipped with an affine connection $
abla$. These are defined in terms of fundamental vector fields on $M$. In a special case, we show that $ho_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma)$ coincides with $ho^{(2)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$, and that $ho^{-}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma,
abla)$ coincides with $ho^{(1)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$. Furthermore, we show that $ho^{+}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma,
abla)$ is related to Clifford structures on $M$.

papers.title: A Gordon--Green-type result for Gorenstein-projective modules
papers.abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a \(\Z\)-graded Artin algebra which is Iwanaga--Gorenstein. We prove that \(\Lambda\) is CM-finite if and only if the category of gradable Gorenstein-projective modules has finite type, and if and only if the lengths of the indecomposable gradable Gorenstein-projective modules are bounded. Moreover, if \(\Lambda\) is CM-finite, then every Gorenstein-projective \(\Lambda\)-module is gradable. These results provide Gorenstein-projective analogues of the corresponding theorems of Gordon--Green for graded Artin algebras of finite representation type.

papers.title: A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories
papers.abstract: By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many indecomposable modules for some tensor product algebras. For some family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ is exactly the subcategory of $\tau$-locally free modules.

papers.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
papers.abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.

papers.title: A topological interpretation of numbers
papers.abstract: We survey recent advancements on the realisation problem for mapping degree sets. In particular, we explain that any finite set containing zero is the mapping degree set between some $n$-manifolds, for each $n\geq3$. Our building factors for the construction of the realising manifolds will be aspherical manifolds. Thus, along the way, we review a couple of open questions related to maps of non-zero degree for aspherical manifolds.

papers.title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
papers.abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.

papers.title: An algebraic proof of Hrushovski's theorem
papers.abstract: In his paper on the Mordell-Lang conjecture, Hrushovski employed techniques from model theory to prove the function field version of the conjecture. In doing so he was able to answer a related question of Voloch, which we refer to henceforth as Hrushovski's theorem. In this paper we shall give an alternative proof of said theorem in the characteristic $p$ setting, but using purely algebro-geometric ideas.

papers.title: Analytic Criteria for Detecting Bernstein-Sato Roots
papers.abstract: We study roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials of ideals. Our first main result gives a general partial differential equation criterion for detecting roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of an ideal. For homogeneous case, we recast this criterion as an analytic condition, connecting the algebraic problem of locating roots with analytic properties of the defining data. As an application, we give a series of roots for the general determinantal ideal prove the strong monodromy conjecture for them. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal variety, monodromy conjecture.

papers.title: Arithmetic jet spaces and the unramified Zilber--Pink conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We show how the methods of delta geometry can be used to bound the degree of points in the Zilber--Pink locus of a subvariety of an abelian variety, if the varieties are defined over a number field and we restrict to points with bounded ramification at a fixed prime.

papers.title: Aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera of K\"ahler varieties
papers.abstract: We study several aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera in K\"ahler families over a smooth curve. First, for a relatively flat coherent sheaf, we characterize local constancy of fiberwise cohomology dimension by equivalent conditions in terms of extension, base change, torsion freeness of higher direct images, and the vanishing of jumping classes. Then, combining this criterion with the K\"ahler minimal model program, we prove invariance of plurigenera for K\"ahler families of threefolds whose central fiber has canonical singularities, and for smooth K\"ahler families of maximal Albanese dimension. We also establish deformation invariance of log plurigenera when the central fiber is projective, and is of log general type. We prove the invariance of higher cohomological plurigenera assuming that the canonical bundle of the total space is semipositive. Finally, we extend Z.~Li--Z.~Wang's deformation invariance result for generalized polarized pairs with abundant nef parts from projective families to Moishezon families.

papers.title: Automorphisms of medium algebras and quasi-anisotropic real affine Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We study automorphisms of Hausel's medium algebras by identifying them with equivariant cohomology algebras of affine Schubert varieties of a complex reductive group $G$. The automorphisms in question are then given by the action of either complex automorphisms or real structures of $G$ on affine Schubert varieties. We focus on describing the fixed points of those automorphisms on the spectra of medium algebras, and prove that the torsion-free quotients of the corresponding coinvariant algebras are isomorphic to equivariant cohomology rings of fixed loci in affine Schubert varieties. In the case of real structures, this naturally leads to and involves the study of affine Grassmannians for quasi-anisotropic (also called quasi-compact) real reductive groups, closely related to recent work of O'Brien. We also discuss relations to automorphisms of Higgs bundle moduli and to symmetric pair variants of medium algebras.

papers.title: Beth companions of finitary essentially algebraic theories
papers.abstract:
For categories, being balanced (meaning that every arrow that is both epic and monic is an isomorphism) can be regarded as a strong tameness property which plays an important role, for example, in algebra and logic.
  We study the problem of associating a balanced companion category, called a \emph{Beth companion}, to a locally finitely presentable category (equivalently, the category of models of a finitary essentially algebraic theory). We show that, if it exists, the Beth companion is unique and can be described in terms of \emph{saturated} objects. Under additional assumptions, we prove that Beth companions can be computed as orthogonality classes, and admit a syntactic presentation via Gabriel--Ulmer duality. Furthermore, we establish conditions for the transfer of properties from a category to its Beth companion.
  A number of examples of categories that do or do not admit a Beth companion are provided. In particular, we show that the category of commutative rings does not admit a Beth companion, and employ Pierce sheaf representations to describe the Beth companion of other classes of rings.

papers.title: Beyond the circle: current algebras, geometry and higher gauge structures
papers.abstract: Replacing the circle by a manifold leads to current Lie algebras and their central and derivation extensions. We separate the coefficient algebra, harmonic analysis and geometric data. Differentials modulo exact forms describe central extensions; divergence-free vector fields give explicit cocycles, whose compatible derivations satisfy a stabilizer equation. Compact examples include the three-sphere and its current--Virasoro extension. We also explain the analytic qualifications for SL(2,R) and its symmetric space and the role of transported multiplication in soft geometries. The recent harmonic constructions of Campoamor-Stursberg, Marrani and Rausch de Traubenberg are compared with the cohomological work of Coquereaux, Frappat, Ragoucy and Sorba and Castellani's loop geometry and infinite-dimensional free differential algebras. A coefficient-algebra construction connects currents to higher brackets and clarifies the additional requirements of a dynamical theory. For Lie algebras of order F, central extensions obey coupled binary and symmetric F-ary conditions, with explicit examples and obstructions.

papers.title: Birational automorphism groups of Severi-Brauer surfaces over the field of rational numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroups of birational automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer surfaces over the field of rational numbers are $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ and $(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^2.$ Moreover, we show that $(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^2$ is contained in $\mathrm{Bir}(V)$ for any Severi--Brauer surface $V$ over a field of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$, and $(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^3$ is contained in $\mathrm{Bir}(V)$ for any Severi--Brauer surface $V$ over a field of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$ which contains a non-trivial cube root of unity.

papers.title: Bornological LB-spaces and idempotent adjunctions
papers.abstract: The notion of an LB-space was introduced by Grothendieck in his 1953 th\`{e}se, referring to a countable colimit of Banach spaces taken within the category of locally convex topological vector spaces, and refining prior work done by Dieudonn\'{e}, Schwartz and K\"othe. Recently, two different notions of `bornological LB-spaces' emerged: one, given by Stempfhuber, refers to countable colimits of Banach spaces as well, but now taken in the category of bornological vector spaces. The other one, given by Bambozzi, Ben-Bassat and Kremnizer, refers to bornologifications of regular LB-spaces, i.e., of LB-spaces in the Grothendieck sense having the additional property that every bounded subset of the colimit is contained and bounded in one of its Banach steps. In this note, we show that the two notions are distinct, but nevertheless closely related. This involves, in particular, an intimate study of the idempotent adjunction of the bornologification and topologification functors.

papers.title: Bridgeland-Enriques general K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: This article introduces a notion of Bridgeland-Enriques general K3 surfaces motivated by the study of Enriques categories over K3 surfaces and the invariant Bridgeland stability conditions. The family of Bridgeland-Enriques general K3 surfaces of degree 10 detects a categorical degeneration of special Gushel-Mukai threefolds. Also, the families of Bridgeland-Enriques general K3 surfaces with higher degrees are closely related to Hodge-special Gushel-Mukai fourfolds and double EPW sextics.

papers.title: Cell decomposition and dual boundary complexes of character varieties
papers.abstract:
The weak geometric P=W conjecture of Katzarkov--Noll--Pandit--Simpson asserts that for any smooth Betti moduli space $\mathcal{M}_B$ of complex dimension $d$ associated to a punctured Riemann surface, the dual boundary complex $\mathbb{D}\partial\mathcal{M}_B$ is homotopy equivalent to a $(d-1)$-sphere. Here, $\mathcal{M}_B$ is a generic $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$-character variety of genus $g$, with prescribed semisimple local monodromies at $k$ punctures.
  In this article, we prove the weak geometric P=W conjecture for all \emph{very generic} $\mathcal{M}_B$, namely when at least one conjugacy class is regular semisimple. A key step is a strengthening of Mellit's cell decomposition theorem: we decompose $\mathcal{M}_B$ itself (without passing to a vector bundle) into locally closed subvarieties which are stably isomorphic to $(\mathbb{C}^{\times})^{d-2b}\times \mathbb{C}^b$. A second ingredient is a motivic characterization of the integral cohomology of dual boundary complexes, developed in [Su24]. Following Simpson's strategy, the proof reduces to an inductive computation of dual boundary complexes arising from this cell decomposition.

papers.title: Cellular Algebra of $A_2$ webs
papers.abstract: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. Thus, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.

papers.title: Characteristic-free Kn\"orrer periodicity
papers.abstract: We show that the Kn\"orrer functor induces an equivalence ${\underline{\operatorname{MCM}}}(R) \simeq {\underline{\operatorname{MCM}}}(A)$ of stable categories of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules, where $R = S/(f)$ is a complete hypersurface ring and $A = S[\![u,v]\!]/(f+uv)$ is the hyperbolic extension of $R$. No hypothesis is placed on the residue field or on its characteristic, $f$ need not define an isolated singularity, and $S$ need not contain a field. This is in contrast to the iterated double branched cover $R^{\sharp\sharp} = S[\![z,w]\!]/(f+z^2+w^2)$, which is stably equivalent to $R$ only in characteristic not equal to $2$. We also give a direct construction of a free resolution identifying $\operatorname{syz}_2^A(M)$ with the image of $M \oplus \operatorname{syz}_1^R M$ under the functor, and an example in characteristic two in which the corresponding statement for the double branched cover $S[\![z]\!]/(f+z^2)$ fails.

papers.title: Cohomology of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Newton Polytopes, Weights, and Boundary Monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\psi$ a nontrivial additive character of $\mathbb F_p$, $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$. For $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ let $\Sigma_n(h)$ be the sum of $\psi_q(u_1^{-1}+\cdots+u_n^{-1})$ over $u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ with $h_1u_1+\cdots+h_nu_n=-\lambda$, an additively twisted average of products of Kloosterman sums. For every $n\ge2$, the cohomology computing $\Sigma_n(h)$ is concentrated in one degree and has dimension $2^n-1$. It has $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$, and its other eigenvalues are the integers $q^{k-1}$, $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, with ballot numbers as multiplicities. The part of top weight forms a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of rank $r(n)$ on the torus $\mathbb G_m^n$. We determine its local monodromy at the coordinate boundary and its determinant: $\det\mathcal W_n$ is the Artin--Schreier sheaf of the sum $-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)$ of the critical values of the phase, twisted by $p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$. The geometric monodromy group of $\mathcal W_n$, and the arithmetic one after normalization to weight $0$, are equal to $\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_{r(n)}:\det(g)^p=1\}$. Consequently the normalized sums become equidistributed like traces of Haar-random elements of $\{g\in\mathrm U(r(n)):\det(g)^p=1\}$. The proofs use Laumon's Fourier transform, middle convolution, the Cayley cubic surface and Larsen's alternative, but no classification of finite groups.

papers.title: Cohomology ring of the strata of holomorphic differentials of genus 3
papers.abstract: We prove that the rational Chow ring of every connected component of the multi-scale compactifications of the genus three strata $\mathcal{H}(4), \mathcal{H}(2,2)$ and $\mathcal{H}(3,1)$ is generated by boundary-stratum classes. Our proof shows Chow-K\"unneth generation property of boundary strata of the multi-scale compactification by reducing the boundary analysis to lower-genus generalized strata of meromorphic differentials, including residueless loci, described through plane-quartic and plane-cubic models. As a consequence, the rational cycle-class map is an isomorphism and the compactifications have no odd rational cohomology.

papers.title: Combinatorics of Mirkovi\'c-Vilonen cycles in twisted affine Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We investigate the explicit geometric and combinatorial structure of Mirkovi\'c-Vilonen (MV) cycles in twisted affine Grassmannians associated with special parahoric group schemes. Using the twist map on configuration spaces of decorated flags, we obtain an explicit parametrization of twisted MV cycles by Lusztig data. We show that the changes between reduced words are governed by the usual Lusztig transformations for the reductive group arising from ramified geometric Satake correspondence. As a consequence, the moment polytopes of twisted MV cycles coincide with the usual MV polytopes for this group. Our construction applies to all special parahoric subgroups in the tamely ramified setting.

papers.title: Cominuscule Richardson varieties
papers.abstract: A Richardson variety in a cominuscule flag variety is defined by a skew shape of boxes. We prove that any cominuscule Richardson variety has a unique decomposition as a product of indecomposable cominuscule Richardson varieties, which are given by the connected components of the skew shape. We also prove that the first Chow group and the Picard group of a cominuscule Richardson variety are dual to each other; both are free abelian groups of rank equal to the number of indecomposable factors. Along the way, we construct an explicit desingularization of any cominuscule Richardson variety of classical Lie type as a tower of (isotropic) Grassmannian bundles. Our results imply that the Hilbert polynomial of the minimal ample line bundle is a well-defined geometric invariant of any cominuscule Richardson variety. We give a positive formula for this Hilbert polynomial.

papers.title: Companion matrices, permutations and lattice ideals
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a novel connection between reductions of companion matrices associated with a symmetric family of certain binomial ideals in the coordinate ring of affine n-space and permutation matrices. Specifically, for fixed monomial orders, we observe that the reduced companion matrices yield permutation matrices satisfying group-theoretic relations. We explore the implications of these reductions, their connections to lattice ideals, and characterize the groups generated by these transformations.

papers.title: Components of discriminants for systems of equations and irreducibility of determinants
papers.abstract: The discriminant of a multivariate polynomial with indeterminate coefficients is not necessarily a hypersurface, and the problem of characterizing its codimension remained open for an extended period. We solve this problem for the discriminants of systems of polynomials with indeterminate coefficients in which the number of equations equals the number of unknowns (square polynomial systems). Such discriminants may have several components of different dimensions. In the space of square matrices, we characterize row-generated subspaces on which the determinant is an irreducible polynomial. This allows us to prove Esterov's conjecture that the discriminant of a nonlinear irreducible square polynomial system is an irreducible hypersurface. Building on this result, we enumerate all components and determine their dimensions and degrees for each of the three conventional formalizations of the notion of a discriminant in this setting (mixed, Cayley, and $A$-discriminants), for square systems and for those overdetermined systems that do not reduce to underdetermined ones. Both the proof of the Esterov conjecture and the descriptions of the three types of discriminants are based on the theory of polymatroids.

papers.title: Computing the Topological Degree of Maps Between 2-Spheres
papers.abstract: We describe an effective method for computing the topological degree of continuous functions $R:S^2 \to S^2$, where $S^2$ is the Riemann sphere. Our approach generalizes the degree formula for rational functions of complex polynomials, $\frac{f}{g}$, without common zeros. To apply our method, it is necessary to represent the function $R$ as the ratio of two continuous complex-valued functions $f$ and $g$ without common zeros. By using the Hopf fibration, this method reduces the problem to computing the winding number of a loop. This enables us to compute the degree of $\frac{f}{g}$ even when $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary continuous complex functions without common zeros, and the fraction has a limit at infinity (which can be finite or infinite). Specifically, if $f$ and $g$ are complex polynomials in $z$ and $\bar{z}$, and the highest-degree homogeneous component of the polynomial with the greater algebraic degree has a finite or infinite limit as $|z|\to\infty$, then the problem reduces to counting the roots of a complex polynomial inside the unit circle, obtained from this component.

papers.title: Conifold gap and all-genus mirror symmetry for local $\mathbb{P}^2$
papers.abstract: The Conifold Gap Conjecture asserts that the polar part of the Gromov-Witten potential of a Calabi-Yau threefold near its conifold locus has a universal expression described by the logarithm of the Barnes $G$-function. In this paper, I prove the Conifold Gap Conjecture for the local projective plane. The proof relates the higher genus conifold Gromov-Witten generating series of local $\mathbb{P}^2$ to the thermodynamics of a certain statistical mechanical ensemble of repulsive particles on the positive half-line. As a corollary, this establishes the all-genus mirror principle for local $\mathbb{P}^2$ through the direct integration of the BCOV holomorphic anomaly equations.

papers.title: Conjugacy classes of regular integer matrices
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the theory of $GL_n({\mathbb Z})$-conjugacy classes of regular integer $n\times n$ matrices and related commutative semigroups. Such a matrix is $GL_n({\mathbb Q})$-conjugate to the companion matrix of its characteristic polynomial. But the set of $GL_n({\mathbb Z})$-conjugacy classes of regular integer matrices with a fixed characteristic polynomial $f$ is usually nontrivial (finite if $f$ has simple roots, infinite if $f$ has multiple roots). It is in 1:1-correspondence to a subsemigroup of a certain quotient semigroup of the commutative semigroup of full lattices in the algebra ${\mathbb Q}[t]/(f)$. In its first part, the paper gives a survey on old and new results on full lattices and orders in a finite dimensional commutative ${\mathbb Q}$-algebra with unit element and on induced semigroups. In its longer second part, the paper applies this theory to many examples, essentially all cases with $n=2$, many cases with $n=3$ and two cases with arbitrary $n$, the case with $n$ different integer eigenvalues and the case of a single $n\times n$ Jordan block.

papers.title: Containment problems for fat point schemes via asymptotic multiplier ideals
papers.abstract:
We study a multiplier-ideal approach to the containment problem for radical ideals of points in projective space. The expected asymptotic multiplier-ideal computation depends on controlling residual base loci of the relevant symbolic linear systems. We isolate this issue in the notion of clean asymptotic multiplier ideals. Under this hypothesis, a failure of \[
  I^{(2r-1)}\not\subseteq I^r \] forces \[
  2r\widehat{\alpha}(I)\geq \alpha(I^{(2r-1)})+3, \] and in particular $\widehat{\alpha}(I)\geq 3$. We show that the dual-Hesse configuration is clean although its symbolic systems have a genuinely non-trivial residual asymptotic base part. We also verify cleanliness for star configurations of lines, giving a further infinite family of non-monomial examples, and formulate a cleanliness conjecture for singular loci of line arrangements.

papers.title: Contravariantly finite resolving subcategories over commutative local rings are trivial ones
papers.abstract: We show that a contravariantly finite resolving subcategory over a henselian local ring must be the subcategory of free modules or the whole module category or the subcategory of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules. This removes the Gorenstein assumption from a theorem of Takahashi. We also show that a resolving subcategory of finite type other than the subcategory of free modules must be the subcategory of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules. As a consequence, every Cohen-Macaulay local ring of finite CM type is uniformly dominant, thereby establishing a stronger form of a conjecture of Takahashi.

papers.title: Correlated Gaussian Moments Determine Polynomials up to Orthogonal Equivalence
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a real polynomial of degree at most $m$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$. We construct finitely many correlated Gaussian moments that determine $P$ up to an orthogonal change of variables. The number of copies and the rational covariance matrices are specified in terms of $d,m$. On coefficient balls, the induced map on orthogonal orbits has a H\"older continuous inverse with an explicit exponent. For $m\geq3$, the normalised local stationary-phase expansion at the critical branch through the origin equals the Gaussian moment series. Its coefficients recover the same finite moment vector, without assumptions on the other critical points. If the leading homogeneous part has an isolated complex critical point, we compute the twisted de Rham ranks and construct formal lattices on each fixed coupling support.

papers.title: Cotangent Bundles as Coadjoint Orbits and Asymptotic Character Formulas
papers.abstract: We present geometric quantization on cotangent bundles as a special instance of Kirillov's orbit method. To this end, the cotangent bundle is realized as a coadjoint orbit of an infinite-dimensional Lie group for a variety of topologies on the dual of its Lie algebra. The group, central to quantum mechanics on manifolds, is the semidirect product constructed from the diffeomorphism group acting on the abelian group of smooth functions on the manifold. We then develop asymptotic character formulas by employing the tangent groupoid of the manifold and investigating the interplay between its groupoid C$^\ast$-algebra and the infinite-dimensional Lie group.

papers.title: Counting irreducible representations of general linear groups and unitary groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a general linear group over $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, or $\mathbb{H}$, or a real unitary group. In this paper, we precisely describe the number of isomorphism classes of irreducible Casselman-Wallach representations of $G$ with a given infinitesimal character and a given associated variety, expressed in terms of certain combinatorial data called painted Young diagrams and assigned Young diagrams.

papers.title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$. Our bound improves on recent work of Habegger, Ostafe and Shparlinski for $n\geq 4$.

papers.title: Degree growth of rational and meromorphic self-maps
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, or a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. We prove that in every codimension, the degree sequence of $f$ differs from its dynamical-degree growth by at most a polynomial factor, with an explicit universal bound on the polynomial exponent. In particular, subexponential but superpolynomial degree growth cannot occur. At a strict dynamical-degree break, we prove the sharper asymptotic \[ \mathrm{deg}_{i,\omega}(f^n)=C_{f,\omega,i}\,\lambda_i(f)^n+O(\eta^n), \] for every $\sqrt{\lambda_{i-1}(f)\lambda_{i+1}(f)}<\eta<\lambda_i(f)$. This extends the degree-asymptotic theorem of Dang--Favre from codimension one in characteristic zero to arbitrary codimension and arbitrary characteristic, and recovers the surface theorem of Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson. Both results rely on a uniform estimate for the temporal discrete logarithmic Laplacian of the degree sequences, obtained by applying the Ptolemy inequality to ordered Hodge--Lorentz packages on varying finite-time orbit spaces.

papers.title: Differential calculus on quantized irreducible flag manifolds
papers.abstract: We give a new description of the differential calculus on the quantized irreducible flag manifold given by Heckenberger-Kolb. We also define a quantum analogue of the Dolbeault complex associated to an equivariant vector bundle on the irreducible flag manifold, and show that its cohomology groups coincide with the cohomology groups given by Andersen-Polo-Wen defined using the induction functor.

papers.title: Dimensions and maximal-dimensional components of higher commuting varieties of symmetric pairs
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathfrak p$ be the $(-1)$-eigenspace of a complex semisimple symmetric pair. For every $r\ge2$, we prove $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))\le \lfloor r\dim\mathfrak p/2\rfloor$ and show that every irreducible component is isotropic for a natural family of alternating forms. For a nonzero Hermitian pair with $\mathfrak g$ simple and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p^-\oplus\mathfrak p^+$, put $d=\dim\mathfrak p^+$ and $\ell=\operatorname{rk}(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k)$. Then \[
  \dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=rd,\qquad
  \dim C_r(\mathfrak p)=\max\{rd,\,2d+(r-1)\ell\}. \] In this case we also determine the maximal-dimensional components of $C_r(\mathfrak p)$; for $r\ge3$, the only maximal-dimensional nilpotent components are $(\mathfrak p^+)^r$ and $(\mathfrak p^-)^r$. For arbitrary symmetric pairs, $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=ra+m$ for all large $r$, where $a$ is the largest dimension of an abelian subspace of $\mathfrak p$ consisting of nilpotent elements and $m$ is the dimension of the variety of such subspaces. Applications give dimension and component formulas for equivariant punctual Quot schemes under explicit framing conditions, and bounds for punctual Gorenstein loci refined by socle parity.

papers.title: Ekedahl's Equivalence Explained
papers.abstract: Ekedahl's theory relates diagonal complexes to \(F\)-gauges, but turning this equivalence into explicit calculations requires careful control of its constructions. These notes explain the equivalence and clarify the generators-and-relations definition of \(\rmt\). At each finite level, we construct bounded projective resolutions of bounded coherent gauge complexes by finite sums of the standard generators. Morita equivalence expresses \(\rmt\) as a tensor product functor. Comparing the constructions across levels yields an exact fully faithful embedding of the diagonal heart into \(\Ch(R)\). Finally, we compute three distinct domino types arising from abelian threefolds that are all supergeneral.

papers.title: Equivariant Homotopy Interleaving and Persistent Whitehead Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group. In this article, we develop some results of equivariant persistent homotopy theory for persistent $G$-spaces. We introduce the notions of $G$-stable and $G$-homotopy invariant distances and define the $G$-homotopy interleaving distance, an equivariant analogue $d^G_{HI}$ of the homotopy interleaving distance of Blumberg and Lesnick. We prove that this distance $d^G_{HI}$ is $G$-stable and $G$-homotopy invariant and establish its universality by showing that it dominates any such distance. We further prove a version of equivariant persistent Whitehead theorem relating interleavings of equivariant persistent homotopy groups to $G$-homotopy interleavings of persistent $G$-spaces. We also prove an equivariant persistent nerve lemma for equivariant good covers of persistent $G$-spaces. As a consequence, we obtain an equivariant weak law of large numbers for filtrations, providing a homotopy-theoretic consistency result for random filtrations equipped with finite group of symmetries.

papers.title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.

papers.title: Every nonsquare integer not equal to $-1$ is a primitive root modulo a positive lower density of primes
papers.abstract: For every integer \(a\) that is neither a square nor \(-1\), we prove that a positive lower density of primes have \(a\) as a primitive root. More precisely, a zero-free half-plane \(\Re s>1-1/N\) for all Dedekind zeta functions gives a lower proportion of at least \(c_a/(N\log N)\), with \(c_a>0\) independent of \(N\ge2\). The theorem of Cureton and Thorner supplies \(N=6000\), so the positive-proportion conclusion is unconditional. The proof uses the marked Type II estimates of OpenAI to count primes $p$ such that $p-1$ is a small cofactor times one large prime. Allowing the cofactor to vary supplies an additional factor of \(\log x\) in the count. We give the counting and sieve deductions in detail and explain the dependence on the zero-free width. The argument gives a lower bound rather than the exact Artin density.

papers.title: Exceptional collections and phantoms of special Dolgachev surfaces
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit description of exceptional collection of maximal length in the derived category $D^b(Y)$ for a particular class of elliptic surfaces $Y$. The existence of non\,-\,trivial semiorthogonal complement (a "\,phantom\,") of this collection is also established.

papers.title: Fourier Coefficients of the Degenerate Eisenstein Series on Symplectic Groups
papers.abstract: We study degenerate Eisenstein series on symplectic groups and construct a new automorphic descent. We show that a certain Fourier coefficient, after restriction to a smaller symplectic group, is itself an Eisenstein series with the same inducing parameter \(s\). We describe the resulting holomorphic section explicitly in terms of the original section and local \(L\)-factors at unramified places. At every regular point of the local descent, we prove surjectivity at non-Archimedean places and dense image at Archimedean places. We finally indicate an application of the iterated descent to maximal Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series.

papers.title: Frobenius liftability of isolated complete intersections
papers.abstract: We classify Frobenius liftable normal isolated complete intersection singularities of dimension at least three over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. In dimension three, they are precisely the regular points and the ordinary double points; in higher dimensions, they are regular. We also characterize Frobenius liftability of the complete local hypersurfaces defined by $xy-g(z,t)$ without assuming that the singularity is isolated. Such a hypersurface is Frobenius liftable if and only if, after a formal change of coordinates, $g$ is a unit times $H^pz^at^b$ with $0\le a,b<p$.

papers.title: Full termination of MMP for klt pairs with big boundaries
papers.abstract: We prove the full termination of the minimal model program for klt pairs with big boundaries. We also prove the finiteness of marked Mori fiber spaces.

papers.title: Functoriality of logarithmic Hochschild homology of log smooth pairs
papers.abstract: The construction of a satisfactory dg category of logarithmic coherent sheaves remains a central open problem in logarithmic geometry. In this paper, we propose an alternative correspondence-theoretic approach based on logarithmic Fourier--Mukai transforms. For smooth proper log pairs, we introduce strong log Fourier--Mukai kernels supported on canonical blow-up compactifications and prove that logarithmic Hochschild homology is functorial with respect to the induced transforms. Unlike the classical setting, logarithmic correspondences do not naturally live on ordinary products, and the standard adjunction formalism fails because of blow-up discrepancies. We overcome these difficulties by constructing explicit unit- and counit-type morphisms that provide the necessary adjunction data without requiring an ambient dg category of logarithmic sheaves. As applications, we construct a dg bicategory of logarithmic correspondences in which logarithmic Hochschild homology and cohomology become categorical invariants. We also define logarithmic Chern characters and a logarithmic Euler pairing compatible with the logarithmic Fourier--Mukai formalism.

papers.title: Galois Orbit Bounds for Surface Degenerations
papers.abstract:
Given a smooth proper family $g : X \to S$ of surfaces over a number field $K \subset \mathbb{C}$, with $S$ an irreducible curve and $\eta \in S$ its generic point, we consider the general problem of constraining the locus $\textrm{NL}(S)$ in $S(\overline{K})$ of points $s$ where the Picard rank of $X_{s}$ is larger than the generic Picard rank. Assuming that the local system $\mathbb{V} = R^{2} g_{*} \mathbb{Z}$ admits a non-trivial monodromy logarithm $N$ at infinity, we give a general condition under which certain points of $\textrm{NL}(S)$ of unexpectedly large Picard rank satisfy a ``Galois-orbit'' height bound. This leads to the following result of Zilber-Pink type:
  Let $g : X \to S$ be a one-parameter family of polarized K3 surfaces admitting a non-trivial limit mixed Hodge structure and such that $S(\mathbb{C})$ contains a Hodge-generic point. Then the locus in $S(\mathbb{C})$ where the Picard rank jumps by $3$ or more is finite.
  Our arguments include a new technique for ``spreading out'' formal geometry, a study of the rigid geometry of equicharacteristic zero semistable surface degenerations, and use the model-free Hyodo-Kato theory of Colmez-Nizio\l.

papers.title: Gauge Origami of the Conifold $\times$ $\mathbb{C}$
papers.abstract: We construct gauge-origami systems on the toric Calabi--Yau fourfold $\mathcal{C}\times\mathbb{C}$ from its brane brick model. Brick matchings and phase boundaries determine elementary D6- and D4-brane framings, respectively, realizing the magnificent-four, tetrahedron-instanton, and spiked-instanton sectors in a unified framed quiver quantum mechanics. We define their partition functions by Jeffrey--Kirwan residues and describe the fixed points in terms of colored BPS crystals. General gauge-origami configurations are obtained by combining these elementary sectors through their common fractional D0-brane quiver. This construction provides a first step toward gauge origami on general toric Calabi--Yau fourfolds.

papers.title: Gelfand--Kirillov dimensions of highest weight modules for basic classical Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We give exact Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimension formulas for simple highest weight modules of the basic classical Lie superalgebras considered in this paper. For the type II orthosymplectic algebras $D(m,n)$ and $B(m,n)$, we identify the PBW associated variety as a product of factor supports evaluated at highest weights for two compatible Borel subalgebras. This gives algorithms for arbitrary complex highest weights, without integrality or typicality hypotheses. In type $B$, the terminal factor is $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$, for which we derive an insertion formula that distinguishes integer and half-integer shifted coordinates. For $G(3)$, $F(4)$ and $D(2,1;\alpha)$, finite odd-reflection procedures give exact formulas, their GK spectra, and finite-dimensionality criteria; we also describe the dependence on $\alpha$ in the last case. In type I, the GK dimension equals that of the simple even highest weight module for the distinguished Borel. The computations use the established ordinary Lie algebra formulas involving Lusztig's $\mathbf a$-function and Robinson--Schensted insertion.

papers.title: Generalized Bogomolov--Gieseker inequalities via Frobenius
papers.abstract:
We establish a Bogomolov--Gieseker-type inequality for tilt-semistable objects on smooth projective varieties of dimension $\geq 3$, in the spirit of the Bayer--Macr\`i--Toda conjecture. A key ingredient is an analysis of the action of the Frobenius morphism on tilt-semistable objects.
  As an application, we prove the Castelnuovo Bound Conjecture, up to an explicit constant term. Combining our results with work of Feyzbakhsh and Thomas, we further show that on a Calabi--Yau threefold, arbitrary rank Donaldson--Thomas invariants of semistable sheaves are determined by rank one invariants, and hence are symplectic invariants.

papers.title: Generalized Kummer surfaces over finite fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a refinement of the Katsura theorem on finite group actions on abelian surfaces such that the quotient is birational to a $K3$ surface. As an application, we compute traces of Frobenius on the Neron--Severi groups of supersingular generalized Kummer surfaces over finite fields.

papers.title: Geometric and homological interpretations of tensor flattenings
papers.abstract: We relate several nonlinear flattenings of structure tensors of finite algebras and modules to their algebraic and homological invariants. Since smoothability of algebras is equivalent to their structure tensors having minimal border rank, this shows equivalence of several tensor-theoretic nonsmoothability certificates to known classical ones. Particularly, we prove two conjectures of Dole\v{z}\'alek and Micha{\l}ek relating the tangency flattening and the $3\times3$ minor flattening to dimensions of tangent spaces to the Hilbert scheme of points. In the process, we generalize the tangency flattening to a mixed regime with two tensor inputs, relating this to dimensions of $\operatorname{Ext}$ modules, and introduce the dual notion of the cotangency flattening, related to dimensions of $\operatorname{Tor}$ modules. In the case of algebras, we also realize the kernel of the dualized tangency flattening within the setting of Harrison cohomology, making the connection to the tangent space of the Hilbert scheme explicit.

papers.title: Global positroid varieties
papers.abstract: Positroid subvarieties of complex Grassmannians are the images of the Richardson subvarieties of the full flag varieties under the natural projection map. Positroid varieties admit natural embeddings into certain quiver Grassmannians for equioriented cyclic quivers. Varying representations of the quiver, one defines global positroid varieties inside the type A global affine Grassmannian. The general fiber of the family is isomorphic to the corresponding classical positroid variety and the special fiber is a subvariety of the juggling variety. We show that the global positroid families are flat and describe their (conjecturally reduced) scheme structures. We also describe the special fibers inside the product of classical positroid varieties and realize the irreducible components of the special fibers in terms of the affine Richardson varieties.

papers.title: Grothendieck ring of varieties and at-the-characteristic numerical invariants
papers.abstract: Assuming a weak form of resolution of singularities in positive characteristic, we show several at-the-characteristic numerical invariants, including Hodge numbers, are given by homomorphisms out of the Grothendieck ring of varieties. Under the same assumption, we obtain two consequences: (i) $\widehat K$-equivalent varieties have the same Hodge numbers, answering a question of de Fernex--Mere; and (ii) universally homeomorphic varieties need not have the same class in the Grothendieck ring of varieties, answering a question of Nicaise--Sebag. In the appendix, we provide unconditional evidence for (i) by proving that birational Calabi--Yau varieties of dimension at most four have the same Hodge numbers.

papers.title: Higher localised $\widehat{A}$-genera: a note on disconnected fixed-point sets
papers.abstract: For a proper cocompact action of a finitely generated discrete group $\Gamma$ on a spin manifold $M$, the higher localised $\widehat{A}$-genera $\widehat{A}_g(M,\omega)$ introduced earlier by the author and Mathai were shown to be an obstruction to $\Gamma$-invariant metrics of positive scalar curvature, for $\omega$ arising from the subring of $H^*(\underline{B}\Gamma,\mathbb{R})$ generated by elements of degree at most $2$, under the assumptions that the fixed-point set $M^g$ is connected and that $g$ is regular with respect to a certain real group $2$-cocycle. We show that both assumptions can be dropped.

papers.title: Higher order Massey products for algebras over algebraic operads
papers.abstract: We introduce higher-order Massey products for algebras over algebraic operads. This extends the work of Fernando Muro on secondary ones. We study their basic properties and behavior with respect to morphisms of algebras and operads and give some connections to formality. We prove that these higher-order operations represent the differentials in a naturally associated operadic Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence. We also study the interplay between particular choices of higher-order Massey products and quasi-isomorphic $\mathcal P_\infty$-structures on the homology of a $\mathcal P$-algebra. We focus on Koszul operads over a characteristic zero field and indicate how our results generalize to the non-Koszul case.

papers.title: Hilbert polynomials of configuration spaces over graphs of circumference at most 1
papers.abstract: The $ k $-configuration space $ B_k\Gamma $ of a topological space $ \Gamma $ is the space of sets of $ k $ distinct points in $ \Gamma $. In this paper, we consider the case where $ \Gamma $ is a graph of circumference at most $1$. We show that for all $ k\ge0 $, the $ i $-th Betti number of $ B_k\Gamma $ is given by a polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in $ k $, called the Hilbert polynomial of $ \Gamma $. We find an expression for the Hilbert polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in terms of those coming from the canonical $1$-bridge decomposition of $ \Gamma $. We also give a combinatorial description of the coefficients of $P_\Gamma^i(k)$.

papers.title: Hodge Theory of $p$-adic analytic varieties: a survey
papers.abstract:
Hodge Theory of $p$-adic analytic varieties was initiated by Tate in his 1967 paper on $p$-divisible groups, where he conjectured the existence of a Hodge-like decomposition for the $p$-adic \'etale cohomology of proper analytic varieties. Tate's conjecture was refined by Fontaine who gave the theory its definite shape. A lot of work has been done for algebraic varieties and a number of proofs of Fontaine's conjectures have been obtained between years 1985 and 2011. But the study of Hodge Theory of $p$-adic analytic varieties started really only in 2011 with Scholze's proof of Tate's conjecture using perfectoid methods. Methods that opened the way to an avalanche of results.
  In this paper, we survey our results and conjectures (comparison theorems and their geometrization, dualities, etc.), focusing on the case of nonproper analytic varieties, where a number of new phenomena occur. We also describe the new objects that appeared along the way.

papers.title: Homotopy Non-Invariance of the String Cobracket
papers.abstract: We prove that the integral string cobracket is not invariant under homotopy equivalences. Using Naef's computation arXiv:2106.11307 of the Goresky--Hingston coproduct and the Leray--Serre spectral sequence for the Borel construction, we compute the degree-two string cobracket for the three-dimensional lens spaces $L(9;1)$ and $L(9;4)$. The rank profiles of the cobracket on their nontrivial free-loop components differ, although the two lens spaces are homotopy equivalent. We also discuss the defect of naturality in relation to the Dennis trace of Whitehead torsion.

papers.title: Homotopy Self-Equivalences of Manifolds
papers.abstract: Hambleton and Kreck described the group of based homotopy self-equivalences of a closed oriented $4$-manifold by a commutative braid of exact sequences built from bordism groups and the Postnikov $2$-type. We construct the analogous braid for closed oriented $BO\langle n+1\rangle$-manifolds $M$ of dimension $2n$ or $2n-1$ whose fundamental group is finite or infinite cyclic and which satisfy one condition on the action of $\pi_1$ on the homotopy of the fibre of $M\to P_n(M)$. We compute $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^1\times S^{m-1})\cong(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$ for $m\ge4$, and $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^3\times S^3)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/12)^2\rtimes SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with the standard action modulo $12$. Further, $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^3\times S^4)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/2\oplus\mathbb{Z}/24)\rtimes(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$ has order $192$, that $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^4\times S^4)\cong D_4\times\mathbb{Z}/2$ has order $16$, and that for connected sums of $r\ge2$ copies of $S^3\times S^3$ the kernel contains a subgroup $(\mathbb{Z}/12)^{2r}$ on which the permutations of the summands act non-trivially. For $S^p\times S^p$ the kernel is a sum of two copies of $\pi_{2p}(S^p)$ modulo Whitehead products with $\iota_p$, and the image is determined by an obstruction on the Whitehead square. In particular $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^5\times S^5)$ is isomorphic to the theta subgroup of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^7\times S^7)$ is an extension of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ by $(\mathbb{Z}/120)^2$.

papers.title: Hopf $2$-cocycles for certain affine algebraic reductive groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a reductive affine algebraic group over $\mathbb C$ with toral identity component $T$ and finite component group $K$. We describe finite indecomposable semisimple module categories over $\Rep(G)$ using equivariant data that incorporate the extension class. We prove that every fiber functor is classical and determine the image of its Hopf $2$-cocycle support in $K$ and its intersection with $T$. This yields a minimality criterion involving a finite stabilizer cocycle and an alternating bicharacter on a sublattice of $\widehat T$ of index at most $|K|$. When $\dim T=1$, every Hopf $2$-cocycle for $G$ has finite support of order at most $|K|^2$. We compute all gauge classes for the split and nonsplit extensions with component group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ and inversion action, and compare the support formulas with the K\"unneth coordinates for commutative direct products. Finally, for an arbitrary reductive group $G$, a minimal Hopf $2$-cocycle in a regular deformation of the trivial Hopf $2$-cocycle forces $G$ to be a torus. This uses locality and rigidity of algebraic matrix coefficients on the semisimple quotient of $G$.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
papers.abstract: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.

papers.title: Improved Upper Bounds for the Rank of the Determinant Tensor via Glynn's Formula
papers.abstract: In this paper, we improve the upper bound for the tensor rank of the $n \times n$ determinant tensor to $\mathcal{B}_n-2^{n-1}+n+1$ by finding a new tensor decomposition of the tensor, where $\mathcal{B}_n$ denotes the $n$-th Bell number.
