The main idea is to replace a part of the tensor decomposition suggested by Houston--Goucher--Johnston with a tensor that is essentially the same as the $n \times n$ permanent tensor, and to use Glynn's formula. This upper bound gives an improved upper bound for the Waring rank of the $n \times n$ determinant polynomial for $n \geq 17$ as well.

papers.title: Infinitely ludic categories
papers.abstract: Pursuing a new approach to the study of infinite games in combinatorics, we introduce the categories $\mathbf{Game}_{A}$ and $\mathbf{Game}_{B}$ and improve some classical results concerning topological games related to the duality between covering properties of $X$ and convergence properties of $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}(X)$ by establishing the existence and key role of certain natural transformations. We describe these ludic categories in various equivalent forms, viewing their objects as certain structured trees, presheaves, or metric spaces, and we thereby obtain their arboreal, functorial and metrical appearances. We use their metrical disguise to demonstrate a universality property of the Banach-Mazur game. The various equivalent descriptions come with underlying functors to more familiar categories which help establishing some important properties of the game categories: they are complete, cocomplete, extensive, cartesian closed, and coregular, but neither regular nor locally cartesian closed. We prove that their classes of strong epimorphisms, of regular epimorphisms, and of descent morphisms, are all distinct, and we show that these categories have weak classifiers for strong partial maps. Some of the categorical constructions have interesting game-theoretic interpretations.

papers.title: Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
papers.abstract: We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $\lambda$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $\lambda$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.

papers.title: Integer decomposition property of three-dimensional smooth polytopes: a shorter proof
papers.abstract: Oda's smoothness conjecture asserts that every smooth lattice polytope has the integer decomposition property. The three-dimensional case of this conjecture was recently proven by AI. Here we give a much shorter proof of this result.

papers.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
papers.abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.

papers.title: Integral cohomology of dual boundary complexes is motivic
papers.abstract: In this note, we give a motivic characterization of the integral cohomology of dual boundary complexes of smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic varieties. As a corollary, the dual boundary complex of any variety stably isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_m^r\times \mathbb{A}^s$ with $s>0$ is contractible. In a separate paper [Su26], this corollary has been used by the author in his proof of the weak geometric P=W conjecture for very generic $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$-character varieties over any punctured Riemann surfaces.

papers.title: Irrational families of Fano weighted complete intersection fourfolds
papers.abstract: We study the irrationality of smooth Fano complete intersection fourfolds in weighted projective spaces, using an atom theoretic approach based solely on Gromov--Witten invariants. We prove symplectic irrationality, and hence irrationality for every smooth member, in a wide range of families for which irrationality was previously known only for very general members.

papers.title: Large condensation in enriched $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that many algebraic features of higher condensation theory are really features of higher algebra. We work in the context of monads on the unit of a monoidal 2- category. Assuming that 2-categorical unstraightening is monoidal, we show that the functor which takes such a monad to its Eilenberg-Moore object is lax monoidal. We use this to introduce an analog of condensation for codimension-i symmetries, without assuming dualizability. We give sufficient conditions for Morita equivalence of endomorphisms of condensates. We relate higher centralizers to iterated categories of modules. Along the way, we prove results pertaining to functoriality of Day convolution for enriched infinity-categories, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Lattice Bruhat intervals are polytopal
papers.abstract: For a Bruhat interval $[x,y]$ in an arbitrary Coxeter group which is a lattice, we give a type-uniform construction of a convex polytope whose complete face lattice realizes $[x,y]$. This gives a polytopal realization of the coincidence between classical Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials for lattice Bruhat intervals and Stanley's toric $g$-polynomials. Consequently, the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial of a lattice Bruhat interval cannot have internal zeros, satisfies a multiplicative strengthening of monotonicity, and obeys the generalized upper bound theorem for polytopes. For lattice Bruhat intervals in finite Weyl groups, we explain the relation with the toric geometry of Richardson varieties and derive formulas for their local and global intersection cohomology, as well as a Boolean criterion for rational smoothness. We conjecture that the coefficients of these Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials form an $M$-sequence.

papers.title: Leading term strandings for webs
papers.abstract: A web is a plane graph encoding an invariant vector in a tensor product of fundamental representations of a quantum group. A stranding of an $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ web is a system of colored oriented curves recording one monomial of the vector it encodes. This article focuses on identifying and constructing leading term strandings, those recording the leading term of a web's vector with respect to a lexicographic order on monomials. We show that every open strand of a leading term stranding is clockwise, so the boundary data of such a stranding is recorded by a row-strict tableau. From a row-strict tableau, we construct a web with a prescribed leading term, and the resulting webs form a web basis. This non recursive construction recovers Fontaine's bases and produces others. For $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ webs with no flat vertices, we identify a leading term stranding using the depths of the faces of the web. Finally, we ask whether any two strandings of a web are connected by a sequence of local moves called strand reversals. We answer this question affirmatively for $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, extending a known result for closed webs to webs with boundary; in particular, a leading term stranding of any $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ web is always reachable from an arbitrary stranding.

papers.title: Level one automorphic representations of an anisotropic exceptional group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$
papers.abstract: Up to isomorphism, there is a unique connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of Lie type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be such a group. In this paper, we study the level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ in the spirit of the work of Chenevier, Renard, and Ta\"ibi. First, we give an explicit formula for the number of these representations having any given archimedean component. For this, we study the automorphism group of the two definite exceptional Jordan algebras of rank $27$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ studied by Gross, as well as the dimension of the invariants of these groups in all irreducible representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$. Then, assuming standard conjectures by Arthur and Langlands for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, we refine this counting by studying the contribution of the representations whose global Arthur parameter has any possible image (or "Sato-Tate group"). This includes a detailed description of all those images, as well as precise statements for the Arthur's multiplicity formula in each case. As a consequence, we obtain a conjectural but explicit formula for the number of algebraic, cuspidal, level one automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{26}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with Sato-Tate group $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$ of any given weight (assumed "$\mathrm{F}_{4}$-regular"). The first example of such representations occurs in motivic weight $36$.

papers.title: Lifting Prym Divisors on a Bielliptic Loop of Loops
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a bielliptic curve over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of odd characteristic or characteristic zero, and let $f \colon \widetilde{C} \to C$ be an \'{e}tale double cover. We prove that, if $f$ specializes to a certain double cover of a loop of loops, then every Prym divisor on the loop of loops lifts to a Prym divisor of the same rank on $\widetilde{C}$. As consequences, we compute the dimension of the Prym-Brill-Noether variety $V^r (C,f)$, show that it is reduced and irreducible when the dimension is positive, and compute its cohomology class.

papers.title: Limiting Hodge Structures for Cubic Hypersurfaces of Secant Type
papers.abstract: The limiting Hodge structure relates the geometric degeneration of varieties to its Hodge-theoretic behavior. We study degenerations of cubic hypersurfaces whose singular central fibers are secant cubics. The pertinent degenerations of cubic threefolds and fourfolds have been extensively studied for compactifying the associated moduli spaces. In the two cases, the secant cubics are constructed by the rational normal quartic and the Veronese surface, respectively. The Veronese surface is a Severi variety, and the rational normal quartic is a hyperplane section of it. In eariler work, we investigated degenerations to the secant cubics of higher-dimensional Severi varieties. Here we study the limiting Hodge structures for degenerations to their hyperplane sections.

papers.title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
papers.abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.

papers.title: Local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects
papers.abstract: We establish local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects in Hom-finite monoidal categories C over an algebraically closed field k. A separability morphism contracts the first two Hochschild cohomology groups without requiring an abelian ambient category. Separable algebra structures and homomorphisms from separable sources have open algebraic-group orbits, and affine Bezout estimates give effective finiteness results. For Frobenius subalgebras, exchange relations replace the source and embedding data by a single self-dual idempotent. We prove that their separable inner-conjugacy classes are open in the exchange locus, yielding a bound of 2^(dim_k(End_C(X))) for any ambient Frobenius algebra X; connectedness gives the same bound on the actual number of subalgebras. As an application, we obtain an effective form of the Etingof-Walton finiteness theorem: every finite-dimensional semisimple Hopf algebra H over C has fewer than 2^(dim_C(H)) left coideal subalgebras. In the unitary setting, we bound E-compatible intermediates of C*-algebra and von Neumann algebra inclusions up to unitary conjugacy, under finite-index and finite-center hypotheses. For irreducible finite-index subfactors N < M, we improve the 9^[M:N] bound of Bakshi-Das-Liu-Ren to fewer than 2^[M:N] intermediate subfactors.

papers.title: Maps between circle bundles: Fiber-preserving, Finiteness and Realization of mapping degree sets
papers.abstract:
Let $E_i$ be an oriented circle bundle over a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M_i$ with $i=1,2$ and assume that $M_2$ is aspherical. We prove the following geometric realization result, which extends the classical result for maps between circle bundles over surfaces to all dimensions $\geq 2$. Let $f\colon E_1\to E_2$ be a map. If the induced homomorphism $f_*$ on $\pi_1$ sends the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_1)$ to the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_2)$, then there is a fiber-preserving map in the homotopy class of $f$.
  Using the above result and a computation of the mapping degree set of fiber-preserving maps between $E_1$ and $E_2$, we obtain the following results on the finiteness and the realization problems of mapping degree sets.
  ($\mathcal F$) The mapping degree set $D(E_1, E_2)$ is finite if $M_2$ is hyperbolic and the Euler class of $E_2$ is not torsion.
  ($\mathcal R$) For any finite set $A$ of integers containing $0$ and any $n>2$, $A$ is the mapping degree set $D(M,N)$ for some closed oriented $n$-manifolds $M$ and $N$.
  Item ($\mathcal F$) extends the previously known $3$-dimensional case to all dimensions $\geq 3$. Item ($\mathcal R$) gives a complete answer to the realization problem on finite sets of integers (containing 0) in all dimensions, including in particular the previously unknown cases in dimensions $ 4$ and $5$.

papers.title: Middle convolution for Lie algebra representations
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a Lie algebra analogue of the middle convolution functor, which is defined on the category of modules over certain Lie algebras, including, as typical motivating examples, free Lie algebras, Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, and the holonomy Lie algebras of complements of hyperplane arrangements. First, we demonstrate that the middle convolution for Lie algebra representations can be regarded as a natural generalization of the infinitesimal analogue of the Long-Moody functor for Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras. Second, we show that our middle convolution recovers the Dettweiler-Reiter additive middle convolution for Fuchsian systems on the punctured Riemann sphere as a special case. Furthermore, we show that when applied to the holonomy Lie algebra of the complement of a hyperplane arrangement, our functor is compatible with Haraoka's middle convolution for logarithmic connections on such complements. Finally, we establish a Riemann-Hilbert correspondence between the middle convolution for the holonomy Lie algebra and the middle convolution for local systems on complements of hyperplane arrangements.

papers.title: Milne's rationality conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for reductions of Hodge classes on abelian varieties: The cohomological realizations of such classes pair rationally with Lefschetz classes (that is, classes in the algebra generated by divisor classes) in complementary codimension. The proof proceeds by establishing a dichotomy for reductions of Weil classes (an expected consequence of the rationality conjecture): Either they are orthogonal to all Lefschetz classes or are themselves Lefschetz classes. The key new input are lifting results of Kisin--Zhou for Hodge-type Shimura varieties. This is a cleaned up version of a preprint produced and released by OpenAI on Oct 6, 2026.

papers.title: Minimal presentations of finite-dimensional representations of pseudocompact algebras
papers.abstract: We give a general formula for minimal projective presentations and for minimal discrete-injective presentations of finite-dimensional modules over basic pseudocompact algebras. We also show that the representation-theoretic g-vector of a module coincides with its DWZ-g-vector. These results generalize the description that Derksen, Weyman and Zelevinsky gave of minimal projective presentations for modules over certain finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras. In particular, we can drop their finiteness assumption, and we may work over fields of arbitrary characteristic.

papers.title: Modular fusion categories with trivial Torelli group actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study modular fusion categories whose mapping class group representations are trivial on the Torelli groups, with particular emphasis on the congruence properties of the resulting representations of $\mathrm{Sp}(2g, \mathbb{Z})$. We prove that, for any $g \ge 3$, the Torelli group is contained in the kernel of the genus-$g$ mapping class group representation $\rho_g$ associated with a modular fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if $\mathcal{C}$ is pointed. This refines the corresponding result in \cite{MW25}. We also characterize the modular fusion categories for which the genus-$2$ Torelli group is contained in $\ker \rho_2$; in particular, categories with isotropic adjoint subcategories belong to this class. Finally, we give a complete classification of modular fusion categories with isotropic adjoint subcategories, and determine the groups $G$ satisfying $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{Vect}_G)$ is 2-Torelli trivial but $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{Vect}_G)_{\mathrm{ad}}$ is not isotropic are precisely 2-Engel groups of nilpotent class 3.

papers.title: Moduli descriptions of v-sheaf local models
papers.abstract: We propose a uniform moduli-theoretic description of the v-sheaf local model $\mathbb{M}_{\mathcal G,\mu}$ for an arbitrary parahoric group scheme $\mathcal G$ and an arbitrary dominant cocharacter $\mu$. Our approach is Tannakian and builds on a new theory of parahoric induced modules. When $\mu$ is minuscule, this framework explains the linear-algebraic conditions arising in the theory of local models of Shimura varieties.

papers.title: Moduli of super-representations of quivers
papers.abstract:
In this note, we construct moduli spaces of super-representations of quivers by extending King's Geometric Invariant Theory (GIT) framework to the super setting. Using the even part of super general linear groups and a parity-shifting operator, we construct moduli spaces that topologically parameterize super-representations of a fixed super-dimension.
  We also outline the construction of super quiver varieties for super-representations of framed quivers (without doubling); and realise super-Grassmannians and super-flag varieties as geometric quotients within this setting.

papers.title: Moduli of weighted stable marked cubic surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $Y(E_n)$ denote the moduli space of pairs $(S,B)$ where $S$ is a del Pezzo surface of degree $9-n$ and $B$ is the labeled (marked) sum of its finitely many lines. When $n=6$, $Y(E_6)$ is the classical moduli space of marked cubic surfaces dating back to the nineteenth century. We describe the compactifications of $Y(E_5)$ and $Y(E_6)$ by Koll\'ar--Shepherd-Barron--Alexeev (KSBA) weighted stable pairs $(S,cB)$. There is a finite wall-and-chamber decomposition of the weight domain $\left(\frac{9-n}{N},1\right]$, and we explicitly identify this decomposition, as well as describe in detail the weighted stable pairs parameterized by the moduli spaces in each chamber. This generalizes the work of Hacking, Keel, and Tevelev constructing the moduli space and its universal family in the weight 1 case, and in particular yields a complete description of the fibers of this family.

papers.title: Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
papers.abstract: A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no braiding. Its comonoid objects are precisely Rota--Baxter cocycle bialgebras. Moreover, the free Rota--Baxter adjunction yields a bimonad and free cocycle bialgebras on ordinary bialgebras, with compatible Hopf structures for connected filtered inputs, in both the associative and commutative settings.

papers.title: Motivic and cohomological stabilisation of the Quot scheme of points
papers.abstract: We prove that the motive of the punctual Quot scheme $\mathrm{Quot}^d(\mathscr O^{\oplus r}_{\mathbb A^n})_0$ stabilises, when $n \to \infty$, to $[\mathrm{Gr}(d-1,\infty)]\cdot \sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\mathbb L^{di}$. We prove that the stable cohomology ring $\mathrm{H}^\ast(\mathrm{Quot}^d(\mathscr{O}^{\oplus r}_{\mathbb{A}^\infty}), \mathbb Z)$ is graded-isomorphic to the ring $\mathbb Z[c_1,\ldots,c_{d}]/(c_d^r)$, where $\mathrm{deg}\,c_i = 2i$, answering in the positive a question of Pandharipande. Finally, we prove that the motive of the nested Hilbert scheme stabilises to the motive of the infinite flag variety and we compute the cohomology ring in the limit.

papers.title: Multiplicity One for Five Strongly Tempered Spherical Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We prove multiplicity one for every irreducible smooth admissible representation in the split forms of Wan-Zhang Models 6-10. Combining the Gelfand-Kazhdan method with nilpotent-wavefront restrictions on Bernstein-finite equivariant distributions, we establish the required symmetries through rational orbit analysis, parabolic descent, stabilizer characters, and conormal arguments. The type-$D_6$ analysis treats both the vector-similitude group of Model 9 and the semispin form arising in the exceptional $E_7$ model. For Model 10, the distribution theorem gives a product bound for periods; the individual multiplicity bound follows from Langlands classification and a vanishing theorem for standard modules induced from nongeneric tempered data on the maximal $E_6$ Levi.

papers.title: Mutations of quivers with 2-cycles
papers.abstract: We develop a mutation theory for quivers with oriented 2-cycles using a structure called a homotopy, defined as a normal subgroupoid of the quiver's fundamental groupoid. This framework extends Fomin-Zelevinsky mutations of 2-acyclic quivers and yields involutive mutations that preserve the fundamental groupoid quotient by the homotopy. It generalizes orbit mutations arising from quiver coverings and allows for infinite mutation sequences even when orbit mutations are obstructed. We further construct quivers with homotopies from triangulations of marked surfaces with colored punctures, and prove that flips correspond to mutations, extending the Fomin-Shapiro-Thurston model to the setting with 2-cycles.

papers.title: Notes on Milnor-Witt K-theory
papers.abstract: These notes develop the foundations of Milnor-Witt K-theory for fields of arbitrary characteristic, without any perfectness assumptions. Extending the work of Morel and Feld, we establish all functorial properties of Milnor-Witt K-theory with careful attention to twists. A main new contribution is the computation of transfers in the general, in particular inseparable, case using Grothendieck (differential) trace maps. The results provide a complete framework for the functoriality axioms of Milnor-Witt modules and form the basis for an upcoming work on Chow-Witt groups with Niels Feld and Fangzhou Jin.

papers.title: Okubo algebras and Exceptional Periodicity: tetracode gradings, root-lattice obstructions and Clifford cones
papers.abstract: The Okubo algebra brings together ternary gradings, integral root frames and rank-three geometry. We examine how these structures extend to the complex Exceptional Periodicity algebras. With $N=4(n+1)$, a tetracode character gives eight nonzero homogeneous components of dimension $t_n=8n+3+2^{4n}$. On a tip, a compatible grading has zero component of dimension $8n-5$ and eight nonzero components of dimension $1+2^{4n-3}$. The arithmetic behaves differently: for $n\geq2$, the lattice $D_N^+$ has no full-rank orthogonal frame of unscaled $A_2$ lattices. We exhibit failures of the Jacobi and Jordan identities and determine the derivations and full automorphism group of the ambient algebra above level one. We also give a Clifford-module proof, with the normalization fixed by root products, of the published realization of EP tips as special Vinberg $H$-algebras. This identifies a positive real form and yields explicit formulas for its cone, cubic, Cholesky coordinates and rational dual invariant. The cone is symmetric exactly at $n=1$. Its determinant-one hypersurface belongs to the known $L(8n,1,0)$ series, whose $r$- and $c$-maps give homogeneous scalar manifolds for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges.

papers.title: On complete intersection projective closures of monomial curves
papers.abstract: We study the complete intersection property of projective closures of affine monomial curves. For monomial curves in the four-dimensional affine space, we give a complete characterization of when the defining ideals of their projective closures are complete intersections. We also investigate when the projective closures are arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay.

papers.title: On finite dimensionality of homology of subalgebras of vector fields
papers.abstract: We show that finite tensor products of modules of tensor fields are Noetherian modules over any graded Lie subalgebra of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^n$. As a corollary, we prove the conjecture of I.\,M. Gelfand, announced at the ICM in Nice in 1970, on the finite-dimensionality of the continuous cohomology of graded Lie subalgebras of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of formal vector fields $\mathcal{W}_n$. We also prove that tensor products of modules of densities are Noetherian over the Witt Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on the punctured line. Moreover, for a weight $\lambda\neq0,1$ every nonzero submodule of the symmetric power $S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$ contains $\Delta^{2N}S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$, where $\Delta$ is the Vandermonde determinant. As a consequence, we show that a conjecture of Etingof implies the conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra on the simplicity of the quotients $U({\mathfrak{vir}})/(C-c)$ of the enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra.

papers.title: On Frobenius rigidity for motivic cohomology
papers.abstract:
We study how motivic and \'etale motivic cohomology of a smooth and proper variety changes under extensions of algebraically closed base fields $k$. With finite coefficients, motivic cohomology is independent of $k$, and \'etale motivic cohomology is independent of $k$ away from the characteristic, but depends on $k$ at the characteristic.
  We then consider the fiber of $F-1$ for $F$ the Frobenius, on motivic cohomology and \'etale motivic cohomology for varieties defined over finite fields. We show that this fiber is independent of $k$ with finite coefficients. In addition, we give some results and examples with integral coefficients.

papers.title: On hidden face contributions of configuration space integrals for long embeddings
papers.abstract: Configuration space integrals are powerful tools for studying the homotopy type of the space of long embeddings in terms of a combinatorial object called a graph complex. It is unknown whether these integrals give a cochain map due to potential obstructions called hidden faces. The purpose of this paper is to address these hidden faces by modifying configuration space integrals: we incorporate the acyclic bar complex of some dg algebra into the original graph complex, without changing its cohomology. Then, we give a cochain map from the new graph complex to the de Rham complex of the space of long embeddings modulo immersions, by combining the original configuration space integrals with Chen's iterated integrals. As the original complex, we choose a modified graph complex so that it is quasi-isomorphic to both the hairy graph complex and a graph complex introduced in the context of embedding calculus.

papers.title: On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
papers.abstract: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.

papers.title: On the computation of the canonical basis for irreducible highest weight $U_q (\mathfrak{gl}_{\infty})$-modules
papers.abstract: We study canonical basis elements in higher-level Fock spaces associated with the quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_\infty)$, which are conjecturally related to Calogero-Moser theory for complex reflection groups. We generalize the Leclerc-Miyachi formula to arbitrary levels by introducing new explicit constructions based on symbols, including a column removal theorem and closed formulas in several cases. These results provide explicit descriptions of canonical basis elements with applications to Calogero-Moser cellular characters and to the decomposition matrices of Ariki-Koike algebras.

papers.title: On the existence of Gorenstein injective covers
papers.abstract: For a locally finitely generated Grothendieck category, we characterise the Gorenstein injective covering property by several equivalent conditions, including closure under coproducts. To complete this characterisation, we construct a countable commutative Noetherian Cohen--Macaulay local ring of dimension one for which this property fails, answering negatively Iacob's question Question 1 whether character modules of Gorenstein injective modules over left Noetherian rings are Gorenstein flat. Using this characterisation, we prove that for Noetherian schemes the covering property is Zariski-local. Moreover, assuming that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathrm{QCoh}(X))$ is a covering class, we establish compatible adjunctions and recollements for homotopy categories of injectives and totally acyclic injective complexes under open restriction. However, this property is not stalk-local: we construct a commutative Noetherian ring $S$ such that $\mathcal{GI}(S_{\mathfrak{p}})$ forms a covering class for all prime ideals $\mathfrak{p}$, but $\mathcal{GI}(S)$ do not form a covering class.

papers.title: On the k-th Milnor and k-th Tjurina Numbers of a Foliation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notions of the $k$-th Milnor number and the $k$-th Tjurina number for a germ of holomorphic foliation on the complex plane with an isolated singularity at the origin. We develop a detailed study of these invariants, establishing explicit formulas and relating them to other indices associated with holomorphic foliations. In particular, we obtain an explicit expression for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation and, as a consequence, a formula for the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function. We analyze their topological behavior, proving that the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant, whereas the $k$-th Tjurina number is not. In dimension two, we provide a positive answer to a conjecture posed by Hussain, Liu, Yau, and Zuo concerning a sharp lower bound for the $k$-th Tjurina number of a weighted homogeneous polynomial. We also present a counterexample to another conjecture of Hussain, Yau, and Zuo regarding the ratio between these invariants. Moreover, we establish a fundamental relation linking the $k$-th Tjurina numbers of a foliation and of an invariant curve via the G\'omez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index, and we extend Teissier's Lemma to the setting of $k$-th polar intersection numbers. In addition, we derive an upper bound for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation in terms of its $k$-th Tjurina number along balanced divisors of separatrices. Finally, for non-dicritical quasi-homogeneous foliations, we obtain a closed formula for their $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers.

papers.title: On the natural transformations of extension functors
papers.abstract: Assume that $n$ is a non-negative integer and $\C$ an $n$-Frobenius category. This paper is concerned with the natural transformations between extension functors on $\C$. The main result of the paper indicates that for any pair of objects $M, N\in \C$, the group of all natural transformations from $\Ext^{n+1}_{\C}(N, -)$ to $\Ext^{n+1}_{\C}(M, -)$ is isomorphic to the quotient group $\Ext^n_{\C}(M, \syz^nN)/{\p}$, where $\p$ is the subgroup consisting of those Yoneda extensions of length $n$ arising as a push-out along a morphism $P\rt\syz^nN$, with $P$ $n$-projective. This result is fruitful from the point of view that, $n$-Frobenius categories may not have projective objects.

papers.title: On the Spectral Synthesis of Lipschitz Vectorizations of Persistence Diagrams
papers.abstract: Persistence diagrams are fundamental descriptors in topological data analysis. Many statistical and machine learning methods require persistence diagrams to be mapped into vector spaces or compared through kernels. Although many persistence diagram vectorizations and persistence kernels have been proposed, there is no general framework for determining which persistence diagram vectorizations are synthesizable. Spectral synthesis asks whether the exponential monomials contained in the translation-invariant variety generated by a function span a dense subspace of that variety. We introduce uniformly discrete spectral synthesis for persistence diagram vectorizations using Fourier analysis on groups of virtual persistence diagrams. When the space of persistence intervals is separable, we prove sufficient conditions for uniformly discrete spectral synthesis and derive approximation results for virtual persistence diagrams with bounded total multiplicity. We then classify many persistence diagram vectorizations and persistence kernels from the literature by uniformly discrete spectral synthesis.

papers.title: On the sphere spectrum from the viewpoint of linear logic
papers.abstract: In this note, we show the category of $\Gamma$-sets with the sphere spectrum, the smash product, and the substitution product gives rise to an isomix linearly distributive category, which is a categorical semantics of the multiplicative fragment of linear logic. We also show Lydakis' assembly map between these two monoidal products corresponds to the mixor.

papers.title: On the triangulated structure of stable monomorphism categories
papers.abstract: We investigate the triangulated structure of stable monomorphism categories (filtered chain categories) over a Frobenius category. The high degree of symmetry of linear quivers leads to a plethora of semiorthogonal decompositions into smaller categories of the same type. These form polygons of recollements, in which a full turn of mutations is a power of a particular auto-equivalence of the stable monomorphism category. A certain power of this auto-equivalence is the square of the suspension functor. We describe the infinite chains of adjoint pairs obtained from the polygons. As an application, we explicate the construction of Bondal and Kapranov for lifting representing objects of dualized hom-functors in our setup.

papers.title: Partially compactified quantum cluster structures on simple algebraic groups and the full Berenstein--Zelevinsky conjecture
papers.abstract: The construction of partially compactified cluster algebras on coordinate rings is handled by using codimension 2 arguments on cluster covers. An analog of this in the quantum situation is highly desirable but has not been found yet. In this paper, we present a general method for the construction of partially compactified quantum cluster algebra structures on quantized coordinate rings from that of quantum cluster algebra structures on localizations. As an application, we construct a partially compactified quantum cluster algebra structure on the quantized coordinate ring of every connected, simply connected complex simple algebraic group. Along the way, we settle in full the Berenstein--Zelevinsky conjecture that all quantum double Bruhat cells have quantum cluster algebra structures associated to seeds indexed by arbitrary signed words, and prove that all such seeds are linked to each by mutations.

papers.title: Pasting and stability in convergence spaces
papers.abstract: We prove a pasting lemma for locally finite closed covers of convergence spaces with limit codomains. We also show how the validity of such lemmas characterizes limit spaces.

papers.title: Plane Cremona maps preserving a Euclidean volume form
papers.abstract: We give a presentation by generators and relations of the group of birational transformations of the plane preserving a differential form with poles along a triple line. This group strictly contains the automorphism group of the affine plane.

papers.title: Pointwise character bounds for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
papers.abstract: We present a basic pointwise bound for the irreducible characters of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ and, as an application, derive new $L^p$ bounds for these characters. Our approach is based on the descent of characters to singular sets and the cancellation in this formula.

papers.title: Polar Degrees of Matroids
papers.abstract: We show that the polar degrees of the coordinate-wise inverse of a linear subspace $L \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ are given by the coefficients of a substitution of the reduced characteristic polynomial of the associated matroid $\mathrm{M}(L)$. Our proof connects the geometry of conormal varieties of reciprocal linear spaces to the combinatorial conormal fan of $\mathrm{M}(L)$. As a corollary, we settle two open conjectures regarding matroid discriminants.

papers.title: Polynomiality for algebras of invariants associated with some In\"on\"u-Wigner contractions in type A
papers.abstract: This paper deals with polynomiality of algebras of symmetric invariants (or generated by symmetric semi-invariants) associated with some particular In\"on\"u-Wigner contractions in type A. More precisely we are interested with contractions of some parabolic subalgebras in type A with respect to their decomposition into their Levi factor and their nilpotent radical, the latter becoming an abelian ideal of the contraction. When the parabolic subalgebra $\mathfrak p$ has its Levi factor decomposing into three blocks, which are symmetric with respect to the antidiagonal, we show in this article that the algebra of symmetric invariants associated with the contraction of the canonical truncation of $\mathfrak p$ has a Weistrass section. It follows that such an algebra of invariants is a polynomial algebra, for which we can give the number of algebraically independent homogeneous generators, their weight and degree. The method relies on the construction of an adapted pair for such a contraction. When the Levi factor of $\mathfrak p$ has its central block not of the same size as its two extremal blocks, we also show that the above algebra of symmetric invariants is equal to the algebra generated by symmetric semi-invariants associated with the In\"on\"u-Wigner contraction of $\mathfrak p$.

papers.title: Projective models for Hilbert squares of $K3$ surfaces
papers.abstract: For a very general polarized $K3$ surface $S\subset \mathbb{P}^g$ of genus $g\ge 5$, we study the linear system on the Hilbert square $S^{[2]}$ associated to quadrics in $\mathbb{P}^g$ that contain $S$. We prove its very ampleness for $g\geq 7$. In the cases of genus 7 or 8, we describe in detail the projective geometry of the corresponding embedding by making use of the Mukai model for $S$. In both cases, it can be realized as a degeneracy locus on an ambient homogeneous space, in a strikingly similar fashion. In consequence, we give explicit descriptions of its ideal and syzygies. Furthermore, we extract new information on the locally complete families, in a first step towards the understanding of their projective geometry.

papers.title: Pseudo-torsion classes
papers.abstract:
For a finite dimensional algebra $\Lambda$, we consider a torsion class $G$ in $mod$-$\Lambda$, which is not necessarily functorially finite. We construct a wall-and-chamber structure for $G$ where the chambers are the connected components of the complement of the union of walls. We call these ``pseudo-chambers''. We also consider ``infinitesimal chambers". To each pseudo-chamber $U$ we associate a ``pseudo-torsion class'' $P(U)$ and a ``pseudo-torsionfree class'' $Q(U)$ and show that they determine $U$. Furthermore, we show that if both $P(U)$ and $Q(U)$ are finitely generated, then $U$ is an open set. We consider ``green paths'' in the stability space and associate to them Harder-Narasimhan stratifications of $G$. This paper is part of a series of papers whose goal is to study the ``ghosts'' which are remnants of the indecomposable $\Lambda$-modules which do not lie in $G$.
  In the special case when our torsion class is all of $mod$-$\Lambda$, we are in the classical well-known setting. All of our results apply to this classical setting. The ``pseudo-torsion classes'' are torsion classes. We point out that we do not take the closure of the set of walls. So, we get more pseudo-chambers and our results are new even in this classical setting.

papers.title: P{\l}onka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{P{\l}onka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for P{\l}onka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.

papers.title: Quadratic Euler Characteristic of Geometrically Cyclic Branched Coverings
papers.abstract:
For an $n$-fold geometrically cyclic branched covering $Y$ of a smooth, projective scheme $X$ branched at a smooth closed subscheme $Z\subset X$ with $n \in k^\times$, we compute the quadratic Euler characteristic of $Y$ in terms of certain Euler classes on $X$ and $Z$ using the quadratic Riemann-Hurwitz formula of Levine. When $n$ is odd, we relate the quadratic Euler characteristic of $Y$ to the quadratic Euler characteristics of $X$ and $Z$, obtaining similar formulae to the situation in topology.
  As an application, we compute the quadratic Euler characteristic of geometrically cyclic branched double coverings of $\mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: Quandles with isomorphic representation categories
papers.abstract: We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).

papers.title: Recollements of derived categories from $n$-term big tilting complexes
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a ring, let ${\bf T}$ be a finite-term big tilting complex over $A$, and choose a bounded projective representative $\cpx{P}$ of ${\bf T}$. Put $B=\End_{\D{A}}(\cpx{P})$. We prove that the kernel of the associated derived tensor functor ${\bf R}:\D{B}\to\D{A}$ is equivalent, through the derived inclusion, to $\D{\mathscr E}$, where $\mathscr E=\Ker({\bf R})\cap B\Modcat$ carries the inherited exact structure. Consequently, $\D{B}$ admits a recollement by $\D{\mathscr E}$ and $\D{A}$. The proof combines a dg double-centralizer argument with a functorial realisation of the kernel on unbounded complexes. The category $\mathscr E$ is definable and $d$-symmetric whenever $d$ is at least the projective amplitude of the underlying perfect right $B$-complex. We also characterise when the kernel is induced by a homological ring epimorphism: this holds precisely when $\mathscr E$ is an abelian subcategory, or equivalently when the standard $t$-structure restricts to the kernel. In amplitude at most one, this recovers the universal-localisation description for two-term big tilting complexes. Over semiperfect endomorphism rings, the amplitude is detected by reduction modulo the Jacobson radical. Finally, we construct non-compact examples of arbitrarily large minimal projective amplitude. One family yields algebraic Calkin quotients; another, over connected rings constructed from singular local hypersurfaces, has nonzero, non-abelian exact kernels and cannot be obtained from modules by derived equivalences between ordinary rings.

papers.title: Reduced characteristic number criteria for $T^k$- and $(\mathbb Z_2)^k$-equivariant bordisms
papers.abstract: Classical equivariant bordism theories require computing the full collection of equivariant characteristic numbers to detect whether an equivariant manifold bounds equivariantly or not. This paper establishes simplified equivariant bordism characterizations for two families of equivariant manifolds with isolated fixed points: unitary $T^k$-manifolds and closed smooth $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^k$-manifolds. For any unitary $T^k$-manifold $M$ with isolated fixed points, we establish an equivariant unitary bordism criterion built entirely from a single polynomial of equivariant Chern classes. We further introduce the minimal distinguishing degree and obtain two key inequalities that capture the interplay between $\dim M$ and the Euler characteristic $\chi(M)$ through this minimal distinguishing degree. These inequalities settle the existence problem of a linear lower bound for $\chi(M)$ within the framework of Kosniowski's conjecture and partially verify the conjecture under natural admissible assumptions. We also provide an alternative proof settling the toric generalization of Kosniowski's conjecture when $\dim M=2k$. By contrast, for a closed smooth $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^k$-manifold with isolated fixed points, we derive a more concise equivariant bordism criterion relying solely on the powers of the top equivariant Stiefel-Whitney class. Our new criteria substantially reduce computational demands.

papers.title: Relative cone of curves and contractions of a successive blowup
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a normal variety in arbitrary characteristic, and let $\tilde X$ be the successive blowup along subvarieties $Z_1,\dotsc,Z_n\subseteq X$ of codimension at least two that have simple normal crossings and satisfy $Z_h\not\supseteq Z_i$ whenever $h<i$. We prove that the relative cone of curves $\overline{\operatorname{NE}}(\tilde X/X)$ is generated by the classes of finitely many elementary curves, and that every face admits a contraction over $X$. Moreover, we prove that every small face contraction admits a $D$-flip for every $\mathbb R$-Cartier divisor $D$ that is relatively anti-ample. We also compute the relative Cox sheaf and prove its finite generation.

papers.title: Remarks on the monodromy conjecture for symmetric determinantal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We compute the local and global Denef--Loeser topological zeta functions of the determinant on the space of symmetric matrices. It verifies the strong monodromy conjecture of the symmetric determinant function. The computation relates to the geometry of complete quadrics and wonderful embeddings.

papers.title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
papers.abstract: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Dousse and F\'eray on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.

papers.title: Root data in character varieties
papers.abstract: Given $G$ an algebraic reductive group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and $\Gamma$ a finitely generated group, we provide a stratification of the $G$-character variety of $\Gamma$ in terms of conjugacy classes of parabolic subgroups of $G$. Each stratum has the structure of a pseudo-quotient, which is a relaxed GIT notion capturing the topology of the quotient and, therefore, behaving well for motivic computations of invariants of the character varieties. These stratifications are constructed by analyzing the root datum of $G$ to encode parabolic classes. Finally, detailed and explicit motivic formulae are provided for cases with Dynkin diagram of types $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$.

papers.title: Rotation fixed points of undecorated braid varieties and fusion rings of affine Lie algebras
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simply connected semisimple algebraic group. On the (undecorated) braid variety associated with a power of a Coxeter element, there is a finite-order autoequivalence, called the Zamolodchikov transformation, induced by cyclic rotation of words. In this paper, we show that the coarse moduli space of the fixed-point stack of this autoequivalence is isomorphic to the spectrum of the fusion ring of the corresponding affine Lie algebra. The above results also extend to twisted Coxeter elements, and the fusion rings of all affine Lie algebras are obtained in this way.

papers.title: Second Chern class and Fujiki constants of hyperk\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We study characteristic classes on hyperk\"ahler manifolds with a view towards the Verbitsky component. The case of the second Chern class leads to a conditional upper bound on the second Betti number in terms of the Riemann--Roch polynomial, which is also valid for singular examples. We discuss the general structure of characteristic classes and the Riemann--Roch polynomial on hyperk\"ahler manifolds using among other things Rozansky--Witten theory.

papers.title: Separating components of real algebraic varieties by cohomological invariants
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth algebraic variety over $\mathbb{R}$. We study the separation of the connected components of $X(\mathbb{R})$ by equivariant cohomology, unramified cohomology, and signatures of unramified quadratic forms. Our results highlight how the geometry of $X$ influences these questions. We apply them to cubic hypersurfaces, complete intersections of two quadrics, abelian varieties, and Enriques surfaces. We also obtain new bounds on the exponent of the cokernel of higher signature morphisms in $\mathbf{I}$-cohomology and investigate the optimality of these bounds for smooth projective varieties.

papers.title: Sharp degree bound for rational proper maps from $\mathbb B^2$ to $\mathbb B^4$
papers.abstract: We prove that every rational proper holomorphic map from $\mathbb{B}^2$ to $\mathbb{B}^4$ has degree at most $5$, confirming D'Angelo's conjecture in this case. This sharp bound follows from Meylan's degree estimates and an intersection-theoretic argument ruling out degree $6$.

papers.title: Sheaves for spacetimes: a survey
papers.abstract: On a spacetime endowed with a time function (such as a globally hyperbolic manifold) we solve the global Cauchy problem for hyperbolic D-modules in the framework of Sato's hyperfunctions, illustrating the effectiveness of microlocal-sheaf theoretic methods in linear problems.

papers.title: Shift orbifolds, decompactification limits, and lattices
papers.abstract: We describe the general shift orbifold of a Narain CFT and use this to investigate decompactification limits in the heterotic Narain moduli space. We also comment on higher rank theories and describe some applications to the CFT based on the Leech lattice and its shift orbifolds.

papers.title: Shifted Symplectic Fibrations and Derived Thurston Theorem
papers.abstract: In classical symplectic geometry, under mild conditions, Thurston proved that one can construct a compatible symplectic form on the total space of a symplectic fibration with a connected symplectic base. Here we prove a derived symplectic analogue of this result, called the derived Thurston theorem. More precisely, we show that if a morphism $\pi: X \rightarrow S$ of derived stacks has a shifted symplectic fibration structure and the target stack $S$ admits a shifted symplectic structure, then, under certain conditions, one can construct a shifted symplectic structure on a dense Zariski-open derived substack of the source stack $X$, compatible with $\pi$ in a sense similar to the classical case. In this derived setting, we also present numerous examples of shifted symplectic fibrations, develop an affine model construction for such fibrations, and provide applications of the derived Thurston theorem.

papers.title: Shifted symplectic structures on derived analytic moduli of $\ell$-adic local systems and Galois representations
papers.abstract:
We develop a characterisation of non-Archimedean derived analytic geometry based on dg enhancements of dagger algebras. This allows us to formulate derived analytic moduli functors for many types of pro-\'etale sheaves, and to construct shifted symplectic structures on them by transgression using arithmetic duality theorems. In order to handle duality functors involving Tate twists, we introduce weighted shifted symplectic structures on formal weighted moduli stacks, with the usual moduli stacks given by taking $\mathbb{G}_m$-invariants.
  In particular, this establishes the existence of shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures on derived moduli stacks of $\ell$-adic constructible complexes on smooth varieties via Poincar\'e duality, and on derived moduli stacks of $\ell$-adic Galois representations via Tate and Poitou--Tate duality; the latter proves a conjecture of Minhyong Kim.
  Unweighted shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures are also established for $\ell$-adic Galois representations of cyclotomic fields $K(\mu_{\ell^{\infty}})$, subject to additional constraints related to Iwasawa theory; these derived moduli stacks yield a non-abelian analogue of Selmer complexes, with $0$-shifted symplectic structures related to generalised Cassels--Tate pairings.

papers.title: Singularities of Amoeba Contours
papers.abstract: We give explicit real-algebraic equations for computing the singularities of amoeba contours, separating degeneracies of the logarithmic critical locus from coincidences of distinct critical lifts. For plane curves, this yields practical systems detecting nodes, cusps, and multiple branches. We also show that maximal sparsity does not maximize contour singularities, even for lattice triangles and parallelograms.

papers.title: Smoothable Gorenstein points via marked schemes and double-generic initial ideals
papers.abstract:
Over an infinite field $K$ with $\mathrm{char}(K)\neq 2,3$, we investigate smoothable Gorenstein $K$-points in a punctual Hilbert scheme and obtain the following results: (i) every $K$-point defined by local Gorenstein $K$-algebras with Hilbert function $(1,7,7,1)$ is smoothable (this is the only case non treated in the range considered by Iarrobino and Kanev in 1999); (ii) the Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}_{16}^7$ has at least $5$ irreducible components. As a byproduct of our study about $\mathrm{Hilb}_{16}^7$ we also find a new elementary component in $\mathrm{Hilb}_{15}^7$.
  We face the problem from a new point of view, that is based on properties of double-generic initial ideals and of marked schemes. The properties of marked schemes give us a simple method to compute the Zariski tangent space to a Hilbert scheme at a given $K$-point, which is very useful in this context. We also test our tools to find the already known result that $K$-points defined by local Gorenstein $K$-algebras with Hilbert function $(1,5,5,1)$ are smoothable. The problem that we consider is strictly related to the study of the irreducibility of the Gorenstein locus in a Hilbert scheme and, more generally, of the irreducibility of a Hilbert scheme, which is a very open question.

papers.title: Some non-trivial cycles of the space of long embeddings detected by configuration space integral invariants using g-loop (g =2, 3) graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give some non-trivial geometric cycles of the space of long embeddings R^j --> R^n (n-j >= 2) modulo immersions. We construct a class of cycles from specific chord diagrams associated with 2-loop or 3-loop hairy graphs. To detect these cycles, we use cocycles obtained by the 2-loop or 3-loop part of modified configuration space integrals using a modified Bott-Cattaneo-Rossi graph complex. We show the non-triviality of the cycles by pairing argument, which is reduced to pairing of graphs with the chord diagrams. As a corollary of the 2-loop part, we provide an alternative proof of the non-finite generation of the (j-1)-th rational homotopy group of the space of long embeddings of codimension two, which Budney--Gabai and Watanabe first established. We also show the non-finite generation of the 2(j-1)-th homotopy group by using the 3-loop part.

papers.title: Square integrable representations and Hecke eigenvalues over a local non-archimedian field
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected semi-simple group over a local non-archimedean field $F$. In this paper we study the action of Hecke operators on the Schwartz space of half-densities on the moduli stack $\bpo$ of $G$-bundles on ${\mathbb P}^1$ endowed with a trivialization at $0$ and $\infty$. This space is a representation of $G(F)\times G(F)$ which contains the regular representation of $G(F)$. We show that this inclusion is an isomorphism on the cuspidal part. In addition we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation $\pi$ of $G(F)$ defines a Hecke eigenvalue. As a byproduct we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation of $G(F)$ with an Iwahori fixed vector defines a ${\mathbb C}$-point on the Calogero-Moser space associated to $G$. We also show that for $G=PGL(N)$ the eigenvalues of certain "simplest non-trivial" Hecke operators are essentially equal to the values of the character of $\pi$ on regular elliptic elements. These results are parallel to some of the results of our previous publication where some analogous statements are proved in the case when $F$ is a finite field.

papers.title: Stability and ribbon bases for the rank-selected homology of geometric lattices
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the representation theoretic stability, in the sense of Thomas Church and Benson Farb, of the rank-selected homology of the Boolean lattice and the partition lattice, proving sharp uniform representation stability bounds in both cases. It proves a conjecture of the first author and Reiner by giving the sharp stability bound for general rank sets for the partition lattice. Along the way, a new homology basis sharing useful features with the polytabloid basis for Specht modules is introduced for the rank-selected homology and for the rank-selected Whitney homology of any geometric lattice, resolving an old open question of Bj\"orner. These bases give a matroid theoretic analogue of Specht modules.

papers.title: Stone Duality for Monads
papers.abstract: We introduce a contravariant idempotent adjunction between (i) the category of ranked monads on $\mathsf{Set}$; and (ii) the category of internal categories and internal retrofunctors in the category of locales. The left adjoint takes a monad $T$-viewed as a notion of computation, following Moggi-to its localic behaviour category $\mathsf{LB}T$. This behaviour category is understood as "the universal transition system" for interacting with $T$: its "objects" are states and the "morphisms" are transitions. On the other hand, the right adjoint takes a localic category $\mathsf{LC}$-similarly understood as a transition system-to the monad $\Gamma\mathsf{LC}$ where $(\Gamma\mathsf{LC})A$ is the set of $A$-indexed families of local sections to the source map which jointly partition the locale of objects. The fixed points of this adjunction consist of (i) hyperaffine-unary monads, i.e., those monads where term $t$ admits a read-only operation $\bar{t}$ predicting the output of $t$; and (ii) ample localic categories, i.e., whose source maps are local homeomorphisms and whose locale of objects are strongly zero-dimensional. The hyperaffine-unary monads arise in earlier works by Johnstone and Garner as a syntactic characterization of those monads with Cartesian closed Eilenberg-Moore categories. This equivalence is the Stone duality for monads; so-called because it further restricts to the classical Stone duality by viewing a Boolean algebra $B$ as a monad of $B$-partitions and the corresponding Stone space as a localic category with only identity morphisms.

papers.title: Stranding $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs
papers.abstract:
Webs are planar directed graphs that encode invariant vectors for tensor products of fundamental $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-representations. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, web calculus is governed by effective reduction rules and well-understood reduced-web bases, but these features break down in higher rank. In this paper we develop a global combinatorial framework for untagged $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs, called \emph{strandings}, which organizes local labeling data into systems of colored directed paths on the web graph.
  Our main result is an explicit state-sum formula for the invariant vector of an untagged web as a weighted sum over its valid strandings. The usual labeling-based construction requires a choice of decomposition into elementary web pieces and a vertex-by-vertex coefficient calculation. Our global reformulation avoids both. We prove that the vectors produced by strandings are $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-invariant, compare the untagged theory with the tagged-web framework of Cautis, Kamnitzer, and Morrison, and use this comparison to obtain a complete set of relations for untagged web graphs. We also give applications of strandings to nonvanishing results, basis constructions from tableaux, and connections with Springer-theoretic combinatorics.

papers.title: Symplectic symmetries of a hypothetical exotic $CP^2$: a potential construction or a nonexistence proof
papers.abstract: This paper is primarily concerned with the existence of a symplectic $4$-manifold, homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $CP^2$, which admits a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism. We reduced the existence of such an exotic $CP^2$ to a question in contact geometry. More concretely, we showed that there are precisely $12$ plumbed manifolds, each equipped with a canonical contact structure associated to the plumbing, such that an exotic $CP^2$ with a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism exists if and only if one of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds admits a certain specific symplectic filling. As the main technical result, we completely determined the order and local representations of a pseudofree symplectic $Z_p$-action for an odd prime $p$ on a rational homology $CP^2$ with positive canonical class. Our result suggests that potentially, there are symplectic $Z_p$-actions which are not a finite automorphism of a fake projective plane. Moreover, we introduced a construction, which, under the minimal assumptions on the symplectic fillings of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds, produces a symplectic $4$-manifold on the Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau line via a reverse-engineering process.

papers.title: The algebraic theory of non-archimedean intertwining periods
papers.abstract: We develop an algebraic theory of local intertwining periods for symmetric pairs $(G,H,\theta)$ over non-archimedean local fields $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and finite-length representations of Levi subgroups of $G$ with coefficients in an algebraically closed field $R$ of characteristic different from the residual characteristic of $F$. For open orbits this algebraic version is essentially contained in the work of Blanc and Delorme. The algebraic theory relies on a crucial new uniqueness result, extending a result of Blanc and Delorme for open periods, which asserts that an admissible intertwining period is the only $H$-equivariant linear form extending the corresponding integral on the space of well-supported sections. Moreover the algebraic construction does not require the unimodularity hypothesis imposed in the work of Matringe--Offen--Yang. When $R=\mathbb{C}$, we also remove this assumption in the classical non-archimedean analytic setting, and prove convergence of intertwining periods for all symmetric spaces. At the same time we extend the context of the whole theory in the following manner: we allow $F$ to be of positive odd characteristic, we allow twisting characters in the periods, and we allow $H$ to lie between $(\mathbb{G}^\theta)^\circ(F)$ and $G^\theta$. Finally, in the algebraic setting, as in the work of Blanc and Delorme on open periods, we obtain explicit bounding polynomials for the singularities of the intertwining period. Such bounds are a key ingredient of a new proof of the cuspidal case of a conjecture of D. Prasad on quaternionic symplectic models.

papers.title: The Baumann--Gaussent--Littelmann Symmetry Conjecture for $SL_3$: The Case $(\omega_1,\omega_1)$
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Baumann--Gaussent--Littelmann for $G = SL_3(\mathbb{C})$ and $\lambda = (\omega_1, \omega_1)$. The proof uses the $L$-perfectness of the Mirkovi\'c--Vilonen basis, the Cartan quotient onto the symmetric square ${\rm Sym}^2 E$ of the standard representation $E$, the diagonal normalization of the transition matrix, and its support properties. We determine the transition matrix on every weight space of $E \otimes E$ and compare it with the transition matrix for the dual sequence $(\omega_2, \omega_2)$ under the Sch\"utzenberger bijection. This is, to the best of our knowledge, the first verification of Conjecture 5.15 beyond type $A_1$.

papers.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
papers.abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers also average to zero. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.

papers.title: The equivariant Ehrhart theory of polytopes with order-two symmetries: Part II
papers.abstract: We give two counterexamples to Stapledon's Effectiveness Conjecture. Each counterexample is a $6$-dimensional lattice polytope with an order-two symmetry whose equivariant $H^*$-series $\varphi[t]$ is a polynomial with one coefficient that is not effective. For polytopes with a symmetry of order two, the goal of this paper is to build up a picture of the landscape of results for when the Effectiveness Conjecture holds. Our main result is a criterion, in terms of the faces of $P$, that determines when the Ehrhart ring of $P$ admits an invariant linear system of parameters of the correct representation type. We use these results to reduce the space of possible counterexamples to one of two cases. A randomised computer search produced counterexamples in each case. We also give an example where the equivariant $H^*$-series is effective but admits no invariant linear system of parameters, neither for $P$ nor any invariant subdivision of it, answering a question of Stapledon in the case of groups of order two.

papers.title: The global exceptional theta correspondence for the dual pair $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times \mathbf{PGL}_{2}$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be the unique (up to isomorphism) connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. A conjectural computation by the author in arxiv:2407.05859 predicts the existence of a family of level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, which are expected to be functorial lifts of cuspidal representations of $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with Hecke eigenforms. In this paper, we study the exceptional theta correspondence for $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, and establish the existence of such a family of automorphic representations for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. Moreover, we show that for the automorphic form on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with any even weight $k\geq 12$, level $N$ cuspidal eigenform, its global theta lift to $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ is non-zero. For the other direction, motivated by the work of Pollack, we develop a notion of "exceptional theta series" on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, arising from certain automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. These theta series are holomorphic modular forms on $\mathbf{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})$, with explicit Fourier expansions, and span the entire space of level one cusp forms.

papers.title: The Green--Griffiths--Lang--Vojta conjecture for commutative algebraic groups with unipotent rank 1
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let $G$ be a commutative algebraic group over $k$ such that the linear part of $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_a$, and let $X$ be a closed subvariety of $G$. We show that the Kawamata locus of $X$ is equal to a Lang-like exceptional locus of $X$, and furthermore, we identify a condition on $X$ that implies that these loci are proper subschemes of $X$. Using this, we prove the strong form of the Green--Griffiths--Lang--Vojta conjecture for closed subvarieties of $\mathbb{G}_a \times A$ where $A$ is an abelian variety.

papers.title: The Hurwitz tree obstruction for the refined local lifting problem
papers.abstract: We prove that the differential Hurwitz tree obstruction for the cyclic $p$-power refined local lifting problem always vanishes. Given a cyclic extension of degree $p^n$ in characteristic $p$ and a lift of its degree-$p^{n-1}$ subextension, we construct a compatible differential Hurwitz tree extending the tree of that lift. Realizing the resulting tree by a cover remains a separate problem.

papers.title: The Quotient of Milnor Number by Tjurina Number of Hypersurface Singularities in Arbitrary Characteristic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity, Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity, and s-multiplicity to establish a sharp upper bound for the quotient of the generalized Milnor numbers and the Tjurina numbers for isolated hypersurface singularities of any dimension in positive characteristic. Using this result, we also derive an upper bound for the quotient of the Milnor numbers $\mu$ and the Tjurina numbers $\tau$ for isolated hypersurface singularities of any dimension in characteristic zero. In particular, as a corollary, we obtain that for an isolated surface singularity $(f,0) \subset (\mathbb{C}^3,0)$, $\frac{\mu(f)}{\tau(f)}< \frac{3}{2}$, which partially answers a conjecture of P. Almir\'{o}n. This is also a weak version of Durfee's conjecture. We have also constructed a family of hypersurface singularities of any dimension for which $\frac{\mu}{\tau}$ tends to the bound we get, which means that the bound is sharp, and at the same time answers an open problem raised by P. Almir\'{o}n.

papers.title: The real and complex Betti realizations of motivic multiplicative Thom spectra
papers.abstract: Real Betti realization is a symmetric monoidal functor from the category of motivic spectra over $\mathbb{R}$ to that of topological spectra, extending the functor that associates to a scheme over $\mathbb{R}$ the space of its real points. In this article, we show that the motivic Thom spectrum functor and the topological one correspond to each other, as symmetric monoidal functors of infinity-categories, under real (and complex) realization. More precisely, we compare the constructions of Bachmann-Hoyois (in the motivic setting) and Ando-Blumberg-Gepner (in the topological setting). In particular, we obtain equivalences of $\mathcal{E}_\infty$-rings between the real realizations of the variants $\mathsf{MGL}$, $\mathsf{MSL}$, and $\mathsf{MSp}$ of algebraic cobordism, and the variants $\mathsf{MO}$, $\mathsf{MSO}$, and $\mathsf{MU}$ of topological cobordism, respectively, and an analogous result for complex realization.

papers.title: The Shafarevich conjecture for varieties with globally generated cotangent
papers.abstract: We prove the Shafarevich conjecture for varieties with globally generated cotangent bundle, subject to mild numerical conditions.

papers.title: Total positivity and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: We define a notion of total positivity for the symmetric space $G/K$ by taking the Hausdorff closure of the image of Lusztig's totally positive part $G_{>0}$ in $G/K$. We introduce double Bruhat cells for the symmetric space and define their totally positive pieces. We prove a cell decomposition of the totally nonnegative symmetric space, give explicit positive parametrizations of all cells, establish closure relations, and show that the transition maps between the two natural families of parametrizations are subtraction-free.

papers.title: Towards non-commutative crepant resolutions of affine toric Gorenstein varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a common generalisation of results by \v{S}penko-Van den Bergh and Iyama-Wemyss that can be used to generate non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of some affine toric Gorenstein varieties. We use and generalise results by Novakovi\'{c} to study NCCRs for affine toric Gorenstein varieties associated to cones over polytopes with interior points. As a special case, we consider the case where the polytope is reflexive with $\le \dim P+2$ vertices, using results of Borisov and Hua to show the existence of NCCRs.

papers.title: Trace-function frames and modularity of genus-one conformal blocks
papers.abstract: The recursive relations and modular transformation laws of trace functions have a common geometric source: conformal blocks on pointed elliptic curves. For a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, CFT-type vertex operator algebra and an irreducible module $W$ of it, we identify the bundle $\mathscr{C}_{\mathbb{H}}(W)$ of one-point conformal blocks over the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ with the trivial bundle of intertwining operators. In particular, bases of intertwining operators give rise to global frames of $\mathscr{C}_{\mathbb{H}}(W)$ via their trace functions. Factorization of conformal-block bundles provides a rank formula used to establish this identification and also yields a geometric proof of basic properties of the fusion ring. Then the modular group $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)$ acts projectively on such a frame, with matrices independent of $\tau \in \mathbb H$. This modular-invariance result recovers that of Zhu for vertex-operator traces and gives a uniform geometric interpretation of the affine and Virasoro intertwining-operator traces studied by Etingof--Kirillov, Krauel--Marks, and Krauel--Shafiq--Wood. The trace frame is horizontal for a natural connection whose projectivization agrees with the pullback of the Damiolini--Gibney--Tarasca connection; after descent, its monodromy gives the modular action.
