With respect to this natural connection, we characterize global horizontal sections in terms of Miyamoto's four conditions. As an application of our results, we realize the cusp form $\Delta$ as a trace function for the affine VOA $L_{\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2}(16,0)$.

papers.title: Twisted local G-wild mapping class groups
papers.abstract:
We consider isomonodromic-deformation parameters of irregular-singular connections on principal G-bundles over complex projective curves: for any connected reductive G, pole order, ramified formal normal form, and twist in the interior of the curve; covering the general setup of meromorphic reductive 2d gauge theory.
  We focus on the formal moduli, studying the deformation spaces of irregular types/classes at each pole: their fundamental groups are the eponymous local G-wild mapping class groups (G-WMCGs), akin to the complex braid groups of hyperplane arrangements \`a la Brou\'e--Malle--Rouquier. We prove that they sit in exact sequences involving `wild' versions of Weyl groups, and we parameterize their isomorphism classes via `Galois-closed' nested sequences of Levi subcosets \`a la Brou\'e--Malle--Michel. This relies on Lehrer--Springer theory, and in the quasigeneric case yields new modular interpretations of complex reflection groups and of Bessis' braid-group lift. The subregular regime still yields complex reflections in `relative' Springer theory, provided an obstruction vanishes in Howlett theory; but in general one exits the reflection realm.
  We also introduce new fission trees to treat structure groups of any classical type, after relating with Bell/Stirling numbers, classifying the resulting hyperplane arrangements and describing the local G-WMCGs explicitly. In particular we single out an infinite family of nonreflection examples in type D: they remain K(pi,1) by work of Amend--Deligne--R\"ohrle, fitting the modular viewpoint of `wild' Teichm\"uller spaces in Boalch's theory of wild curves.
  Finally, we extend all of this to the interior twists. Algebraically, this yields a nonsplit setup where the Weyl group is twisted by an infinitesimal outer automorphism of G, so that fission takes place in a proper reflection coset.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Torus Action on the Quadric Threefold and GW-DT-GV Correspondence
papers.abstract: We compute Gromov--Witten (GW) and Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants (including descendant invariants) for local CY $4$-folds over a smooth quadric threefold $Q$, up to degree $4$. We use the virtual localization formula with respect to a two-dimensional torus action to compute DT invariants. Combining these results with the computation of the J-function of the variety $Q$, we confirm the correspondence between DT and Gopakumar--Vafa invariants suggested by Cao--Maulik--Toda in genus zero. Based on these results, we predict a genus one BPS invariant on $Q$.

papers.title: Une conjecture $C_{\rm st}$ pour la cohomologie \`a support compact
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{B}$ be the ring of analytic functions on the Fargues-Fontaine curve $Y_{\rm FF}$. We shaw that, by adding sufficiently iterated periods, one can kill its Galois cohomology in degrees $\geq 1$. For $\mathbf{B}_{\rm dR}^+$, the corresponding result is obtained by adjoining just $\log t$ and is folklore. This allows to formulate $C_{\rm dR}$ and $C_{\rm st}$ conjectures for the compactly supported cohomology of $p$-adic analytic varieties.

papers.title: Uniqueness and non-uniqueness of deriving transformations
papers.abstract: A differential category is an additive symmetric monoidal category with an algebra modality, axiomatizing smooth functions, and a deriving transformation, axiomatizing the differentiation of these smooth functions. An algebra modality may or may not have both the nullary and the binary Seely isomorphisms. Lemay proved that if an algebra modality has both Seely isomorphisms, then it has at most one deriving transformation. It was then an open problem whether every algebra modality has at most one deriving transformation. We answer this question in the negative by constructing algebra modalities with infinite sets of deriving transformations. We also clarify the relations between the nullary Seely isomorphism, the binary Seely isomorphism, and uniqueness of deriving transformations (that is, the property for an algebra modality to have at most one deriving transformation). First, we refine Lemay's theorem by removing the assumption of the nullary Seely isomorphism. Then, we show by means of various examples that the six combinations of absence or presence of nullary Seely isomorphism, binary Seely isomorphism, and uniqueness of deriving transformations, which are not already ruled out by the refined uniqueness theorem, can be realized.

papers.title: Updating zigzag representatives efficiently
papers.abstract: Computation of zigzag persistence has progressed in recent years, with results showing that complexities of many problems closely align with those in the non-zigzag setting. The major efficiency gap now lies in the updating of zigzag representatives. In this paper, we propose efficient algorithms for updating zigzag representatives based on a recent algorithm for extracting zigzag representatives from a $R=DV$ decomposition of a constructed non-zigzag. The main difficulty for designing our update algorithms lies in the adjacency change occurring in two operations that lengthen or shorten a filtration. Despite the adjacency change, we find that the update can still be done efficiently in quadratic time.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the Comon Rank Gap of Real Symmetric Third-Order Tensors
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a nonzero real symmetric third-order tensor. Denote by $r(T)$ its CP rank, by $s(T)$ its symmetric rank, by $d(T)$ its essential dimension, and put $e(T)=r(T)-d(T)$. We establish two complementary upper bounds for the Comon rank gap $$\Delta(T):= s(T)-r(T)\leq\min\{C_{ec}(e(T)),\ C_{dc}(d(T))\}.$$ The excess-controlled function $C_{ec}(e)$ is zero for $0\leq e\leq3$ and equals $9e-3$ for $e\geq4$. In particular, the equality $C_{ec}(e(T))=0$ for $0\leq e\leq3$ extends Friedland's flattening-rank criterion for real symmetric third-order tensors by two additional rank layers. The dimension-controlled function $C_{dc}(d)$ is zero for $d=0$, equals $(d^2-4d+10)/3$ for $1\leq d\leq18$, and equals $d^2/4+d/4+3/2$ for $d\geq19$. The excess estimate follows from the alternating equations and decomposable-bivector support geometry; a low-wedge descent gives the vanishing range $e\leq3$. The dimension estimate combines a transverse polar-completion bound with a shifted estimate for the maximum real Waring rank. Thus the two bounds measure different features of the same tensor and remain effective in complementary regimes.

papers.title: Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms
papers.abstract: The complete intersection forms are the homogeneous polynomials whose annihilator ideal or the Macaulay dual, is an Artinian complete intersection ideal. In this paper, we compute the Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms. As an application, we compute the Waring rank of binomials whose annihilator is a complete intersection ideal. Further, we also compute the Waring rank of the product of binary forms in different sets of variables.

papers.title: What kind of linearly distributive category do polynomial functors form?
papers.abstract:
This paper has two purposes. The first is to extend the theory of linearly distributive categories by considering the structures that emerge in a special case: the normal duoidal category $(\mathsf{Poly} ,\mathcal{y}, \otimes, \triangleleft )$ of polynomial functors under Dirichlet and substitution product. This is an isomix LDC which is neither $*$-autonomous nor fully symmetric. The additional structures of interest here are a closure for $\otimes$ and a co-closure for $\triangleleft$, making $\mathsf{Poly}$ a bi-closed LDC, which is a notion we introduce in this paper.
  The second purpose is to use $\mathsf{Poly}$ as a source of examples and intuition about various structures that can occur in the setting of LDCs, including duals, cores, linear monoids, and others, as well as how these generalize to the non-symmetric setting. To that end, we characterize the linearly dual objects in $\mathsf{Poly}$: every linear polynomial has a right dual which is a representable. It turns out that the linear and representable polynomials also form the left and right cores of $\mathsf{Poly}$. Finally, we provide examples of linear monoids, linear comonoids, and linear bialgebras in $\mathsf{Poly}$.
